ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Exploring the Effectiveness of Trajectory KL Constraint Relaxation
PROPOSAL: Investigate whether a relaxation of the trajectory KL constraint between denoising trajectories can achieve stable training while maintaining control over the marginal KL divergence. To this end, propose a relaxation involving a weighted KL divergence between sampled trajectories and a simplified target distribution, which does not require exact computation of the marginal likelihood. We will fine-tune a pre-trained diffusion model on a held-out validation set task, comparing the effect of exact KL regularization, no KL regularization, and this relaxation. Specifically, we'll use the DPM++ model on the datasets for text-to-image generation (CIFAR10-GAN), document layout generation (ADEMORA), and molecule generation (ZINC 250k).
CONTROLS: Exact KL regularization baseline (KL term computed using sampling), No KL regularization baseline (unregularized PPO training)
COST: 6,720
PREDICTION: We expect the relaxation to achieve better stability than exact KL regularization, and moderately better performance than no regularization, while dealing with the initial value function bias problem.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models via Policy Gradients with Auxiliary Learning
PROPOSAL: Combine the KL-regularized reward maximization approach with an auxiliary learning objective to improve the learning stability and sample quality of fine-tuned diffusion models. The auxiliary learning objective is based on a selected discriminative task (e.g., classification or image segmentation) that is relevant to the downstream application. We will add an additional term to the PPO loss, encouraging the diffusion model to generate data points that are discriminatively valuable according to the discriminative task, thereby constraining the sample generation process towards higher-value samples. For this experiment, we'll apply the DPM++ model on held-out validation sets of text-to-image generation (CIFAR10-GAN), document layout generation (ADEMORA), and molecule generation (ZINC 250k), using the CelebA-HQ and CIFAR10 classifications as auxiliary tasks.
CONTROLS: Baseline experiments without auxiliary learning, Effective sampling baseline using IG-FNN estimation of the marginal KL divergence
COST: 26,700
PREDICTION: We expect the auxiliary learning objective to improve the stability and performance of fine-tuned diffusion models by exploiting the informative structure provided by auxiliary tasks, and to enable better generalization to new unseen data.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models via Policy Gradients with Auxiliary Learning
PROPOSAL: Modify the auxiliary learning objective in the policy gradient approach to leverage the diffusion model's inherent structure by using the progression of intermediate noisy states along the denoising trajectory. This involves learning multiple sequential discriminative tasks at different denoising steps, which encourages the diffusion model to not only generate samples that are discriminatively valuable but also to guide the denoising process towards progressively improving the sample quality. To evaluate this, we will apply the modified DPM++ model on held-out validation sets of text-to-image generation (CIFAR10-GAN), document layout generation (ADEMORA), and molecule generation (ZINC 250k), adapting the auxiliary learning objectives for each denoising step to the specific setup.
CONTROLS: The original baseline experiment without auxiliary learning, Effective sampling baseline using IG-FNN estimation of the marginal KL divergence
COST: 33,250
PREDICTION: We expect this approach to improve the convergence and efficiency of the policy gradient optimization by leveraging the diffusion model's inherent sequential structure, leading to better sample quality and improved generalization to unseen data.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Leveraging the Reverse Process for Efficient KL-Regularized Reward Maximization
PROPOSAL: Investigate a more efficient KL regularization strategy for diffusion models by directly learning the reverse process of the pre-trained diffusion model, thereby considering the denoising trajectory as a single unit. This involves modifying the KL-regularization term to use the reverse process as an intermediate distribution, rather than relying on the marginal KL divergence. We will fine-tune pre-trained diffusion models on various validation tasks, comparing the performance of the proposed approach with the standard KL-regularization scheme and a relaxation-based approach. This will be applied on text-to-image generation (CIFAR10-GAN), document layout generation (ADEMORA), and molecule generation (ZINC 250k) using the DPM++ model.
CONTROLS: Baseline experiments using the standard KL-regularization scheme, the relaxation-based approach
COST: 16,560
PREDICTION: We expect the proposed approach to exhibit better convergence and stability in fine-tuning the diffusion model, as it avoids the marginal KL divergence approximation, while providing more informative regularization to the policy gradient optimization.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Evaluating Fine-Tuning via Rejection Sampling for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Investigate the fine-tuning of pre-trained diffusion models using rejection sampling and analyze its performance on various downstream applications, specifically text-to-image generation (CIFAR10-GAN), document layout generation (ADEMORA), and molecule generation (ZINC 250k). This involves implementing a rejection sampling framework that filters low-reward samples according to their reward associated with a particular loss or comparison, and trains on the high-reward samples obtained. We will compare the quality and diversity of generated samples between the rejection sampling baseline, the standard KL regularization, and a comparative policy gradient approach without explicit reward.
CONTROLS: Baseline experiments for rejection sampling, standard KL regularization, a comparative policy gradient approach without explicit reward; ablations on filter threshold and reward scale.
COST: 40,000
PREDICTION: We expect rejection sampling to yield visually pleasing samples that often generalize well to downstream applications, despite occasional instability and high sample variability, compared to the other two approaches, while the performance gap may vary depending on the evaluation metric used.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Investigating the Minimum Information Principle for Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: Explore the potential application of the minimum information principle (MIP) for fine-tuning pre-trained diffusion models. The MIP states that the most efficient probabilistic representation is the one that minimizes the mutual information between the encoding and the input. We'll incorporate the MIP principle into the diffusion model's fine-tuning process by introducing an additional penalty term to the PPO loss that explicitly encourages minimizing the mutual information between the denoising trajectory and the input data. This can be evaluated on held-out validation sets of text-to-image generation (CIFAR10-GAN), document layout generation (ADEMORA), and molecule generation (ZINC 250k).
CONTROLS: Baseline experiments using the standard PPO loss, a relaxation-based approach to MIP
COST: 20,000
PREDICTION: We expect the MIP approach to yield theoretically grounded and effective regularization, that encourages the diffusion model to maintain the most amount of information about the input in the lowest amount of noise possible, thus potentially leading to more robust and generalizable models.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Fine-Tuning Flow Models for Correcting Pre-Training Errors without Explicit Reward
PROPOSAL: Investigate the possibility of fine-tuning pre-trained flow models, without using explicit rewards, to correct pre-training errors and align the generated samples with the target data distribution. We'll focus on using Langevin dynamics for fine-tuning, which is a locally optimal procedure for the training of posterior distributions. This involves adapting the flow model to directly maximize the log-likelihood of a reference dataset, potentially enabling correction of discretization errors and statistical errors of imperfect learning. Performance evaluation will be done on text-to-image generation (CIFAR10-GAN), document layout generation (ADEMORA), and molecule generation (ZINC 250k) using the RealNVP model.
CONTROLS: Baseline experiments fine-tuning with explicit rewards, baseline experiments fine-tuning without any explicit loss function
COST: 67,200
PREDICTION: We expect the Langevin dynamics approach to enable effective correction of pre-training errors without explicit rewards, while avoiding the initial value function bias problem and leveraging the structure of the flow model to achieve more accurate and stable fine-tuning.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Leveraging the Reverse Process for Efficient KL-Regularized Reward Maximization
PROPOSAL: Extend the scope of the relaxation used in the reverse process for efficient KL-regularized reward maximization by exploring the range of simplified distributions and weighting schemes. This entails varying the form and schedule of the weighting terms to better frame the KL-regularization process and optimize the learning dynamics of the diffusion model. We will apply this approach to pre-trained DPM++ models fine-tuned on held-out validation sets of text-to-image generation (CIFAR10-GAN), document layout generation (ADEMORA), and molecule generation (ZINC 250k).
CONTROLS: Baseline experiments using the original relaxation approach, the modified relaxation approach with varying simplified distributions and weighting schemes; ablations on weighting schedules and tuning hyperparameters.
COST: 40,000
PREDICTION: We expect the extension to lead to a more flexible and adaptable relaxation scheme, better suited to handle the complexities of fine-tuning diffusion models and yielding improved performance on various downstream applications.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE: Theoretical Analysis of Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning via Policy Gradients
PROPOSAL: Investigate the theoretical properties of policy gradient fine-tuning for diffusion models, focusing on the convergence guarantees and bounds on the performance of the fine-tuned model. This involves leveraging recent advances in the analysis of policy gradient methods and exploring novel arguments tailored to the stochastic setting of diffusion modeling. We aim to provide limiting results under general conditions on the reward function and the pre-trained diffusion model, characterizing the trade-off between exploration and exploitation in the policy gradient optimization.
CONTROLS: Comparison with theoretical results for standard KL regularization and relaxation-based approaches.
COST: 83,400
PREDICTION: We expect the theoretical analysis to provide insights into the behavior of policy gradient fine-tuning and shed light on the design of efficient learning algorithms for diffusion models, identifying optimal hyperparameter choices and promising approaches for faster convergence and improved performance.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 8
TITLE: Adaptive Scheduling of Trajectory Reconstructions for Effective Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: Investigate an adaptive scheduling mechanism for reconstructing and refining the denoising trajectory during policy gradient fine-tuning of pre-trained diffusion models. This adaptive procedure adjusts the frequency and scope of trajectory reconstructions in response to the optimization dynamics, aiming to strike a balance between supporting the exploration-exploitation trade-off and maintaining computational efficiency. We will implement this strategy on held-out validation sets of text-to-image generation (CIFAR10-GAN), document layout generation (ADEMORA), and molecule generation (ZINC 250k) using DPM++ models.
CONTROLS: Baseline experiments without adaptive scheduling, basic static schedules for trajectory reconstruction.
COST: 133,000
PREDICTION: We expect the adaptive scheduling approach to enhance the learning efficiency and robustness of policy gradient fine-tuning by closely monitoring the optimization dynamics and adjusting the sampling process on the fly, thus leading to significant improvements in sample quality and diversity.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Invertible KL Regularization for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Train a diffusion model on a text-to-image generation task using an invertible KL regularization scheme, where the KL divergence is approximated by the reverse process of the denoising trajectory. This involves training a reverse process to match the pre-trained model's reverse process distribution, and then using this reverse process to compute an approximation of the KL divergence.
CONTROLS: Baseline: No KL regularization. Ablation: Using the exact KL divergence computation (not possible in practice, but used to illustrate the effect of the invertible KL scheme).
COST: 1656
PREDICTION: This scheme should improve stability and convergence speed compared to ignoring the KL regularization term, but may not achieve optimal results due to the approximation involved.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unbiased KL-Divergence Estimation for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We propose to develop a surrogate for the intractable marginal KL divergence by approximating it with a discrete KL divergence over the intermediate noisy states produced by the diffusion model. This will be done by coupling the noise schedules of the pre-trained and fine-tuned models and applying a kernelized variant of the Hutchinson trace estimator to approximate the KL divergence between the two.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: ignore the KL regularization, Baseline 2: use a fixed KL regularization strength using a trajectory KL divergence, Baseline 3: use a fixed KL regularization strength with pseudo-marginal MCMC toestimate the marginal KL divergence.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: This approach should yield better fine-tuning results compared to ignoring the KL term, while remaining computationally efficient. Potential issues may arise from the choice of kernel and the approximation's bias-variance tradeoff.

This will be done by adding a loss term that encourages the fine-tuned model to produce intermediate states that are close to those generated by the pre-trained model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unbiased KL-Divergence Estimation for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We propose to develop a surrogate for the intractable marginal KL divergence by approximating it with a discrete KL divergence over the intermediate noisy states produced by the diffusion model. This will be done by coupling the noise schedules of the pre-trained and fine-tuned models and applying a kernelized variant of the Hutchinson trace estimator to approximate the KL divergence between the two.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: ignore the KL regularization, Baseline 2: use a fixed KL regularization strength using a trajectory KL divergence, Baseline 3: use a fixed KL regularization strength with pseudo-marginal MCMC toestimate the marginal KL divergence.
COST: 2700
PREDICTION: This approach should yield better fine-tuning results compared to ignoring the KL term, while remaining computationally efficient. Potential issues may arise from the choice of kernel and the approximation's bias-variance tradeoff.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Leverage Intermediate Noise for Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: We propose to develop a novel fine-tuning algorithm that explicitly leverages the intermediate noisy states produced by the diffusion model. By training a modification to the denoising process that compensates for the discrepancies between the pre-trained and fine-tuned models' distributions, we aim to improve the fine-tuning process. This will be done by adding a loss term that encourages the fine-tuned model to produce intermediate states that are close to those generated by the pre-trained model.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: ignore the KL regularization (Proposal 1), Baseline 2: use a fixed KL regularization strength (Proposal 1), Baseline 3: Best-of-N sampling for the pre-trained model.
COST: 18000
PREDICTION: This approach should take advantage of the intermediate noisy states to improve fine-tuning, but the additional computational cost may offset the benefits for large-scale settings.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Leverage Intermediate Noise for Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: We revise Proposal 2 by incorporating a novel intermediate noise interleaving strategy, where we alternate between two noise levels to better capture the nuances of the pre-trained model's distribution and the fine-tuned model's distribution. This interleaving strategy will be optimized during fine-tuning, allowing the model to adapt to the changing noise level and improve the generated samples.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: ignore the KL regularization (Proposal 1), Baseline 2: use a fixed KL regularization strength (Proposal 1), Baseline 3: original Leverage Intermediate Noise for Fine-Tuning without interleaving, Baseline 4: Best-of-N sampling for the pre-trained model.
COST: 36000
PREDICTION: This revised approach should improve the fine-tuning results by better adapting to the changing noise levels, but the increased computational cost may lead to slower convergence or decreased stability.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Unbiased KL-Divergence Estimation for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We revise Proposal 1 by incorporating a simulations-based method to learn the probability flow between the intermediate noisy states, allowing for more accurate estimation of the marginal KL divergence. This will be achieved through neural transport networks that model the probability flows between the intermediate states.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: ignore the KL regularization (original Proposal 2), Baseline 2: use a fixed KL regularization strength (original Proposal 2), Baseline 3: original Unbiased KL-Divergence Estimation, Baseline 4: KL divergence between entire denoising trajectories (trajectory KL constraint).
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: This revised approach should improve the estimation of the marginal KL divergence, reducing the impact of the initial value function bias problem. However, the added complexity may lead to increased training time or instability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical KL-Regularization for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We propose a hierarchical KL-regularization approach for fine-tuning diffusion models, where the KL regularization is applied at various scales of the denoising process. This will be achieved by introducing a hierarchical noise schedule and a nested KL divergence estimation procedure, allowing for more flexible adaptation to the fine-tuned model's distribution.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: ignore the KL regularization (Proposal 1), Baseline 2: use a fixed KL regularization strength (Proposal 1), Baseline 3: Leverage Intermediate Noise for Fine-Tuning (Proposal 2 with interleaving), Baseline 4: Best-of-N sampling for the pre-trained model.
COST: 42000
PREDICTION: This approach should allow for more nuanced adaptation to the fine-tuned model's distribution, potentially improving fine-tuning results. However, the added complexity may lead to increased training time or decreased stability in large-scale settings.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Actor-Critic Learning with KL-Regularization for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We propose to adapt the actor-critic learning framework to the context of diffusion models, where the critic is responsible for estimating the marginal KL divergence between the pre-trained and fine-tuned models' distributions, while the actor is responsible for adapting the fine-tuned model's distribution to the reward signal. This will be achieved through a novel combination of neural transport networks and policy gradient methods.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: ignore the KL regularization (Proposal 1), Baseline 2: use a fixed KL regularization strength (Proposal 1), Baseline 3: Leverage Intermediate Noise for Fine-Tuning (Proposal 2 with interleaving), Baseline 4: Hierarchical KL-Regularization for Diffusion Models (Proposal 3), Best-of-N sampling for the pre-trained model.
COST: 72000
PREDICTION: This approach should leverage the strengths of both actor-critic learning and KL-regularization to achieve more effective fine-tuning results. However, the added complexity may lead to increased training time or decreased stability in large-scale settings.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Directly Correcting Flow Model Errors with Probabilistic Regulation
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel approach for correcting flow model errors without explicit reward signals, where a probabilistic regulation mechanism is introduced to directly adjust the flow model's distribution to align with the target data distribution. This will be achieved through a probabilistic transport network that models the flow between the flow model's and target distributions.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: ignore the KL regularization (Proposal 1), Baseline 2: use a fixed KL regularization strength (Proposal 1), Baseline 3: Leverage Intermediate Noise for Fine-Tuning (Proposal 2 with interleaving), Baseline 4: Hierarchical KL-Regularization for Diffusion Models (Proposal 3), Baseline 5: Best-of-N sampling for the pre-trained model, Baseline 6 (for direct comparison with reinforcement learning-based methods) - directly optimizing the reward function with standard reinforcement learning methods
COST: 50400
PREDICTION: This approach should allow for direct correction of flow model errors without explicit reward signals, potentially improving sample quality at a reasonable cost in generation compute. However, the added complexity may lead to increased training time or decreased stability in large-scale settings.

TITLE: Meta-Learning for Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We propose a meta-learning approach for fine-tuning diffusion models, where a meta-model is trained to adjust the fine-tuning process based on the specific reward or data distribution. This will be achieved through a gradient-based optimization mechanism that adapts the fine-tuning process to the new task, allowing for more efficient and effective fine-tuning.

PREDICTION: This approach should allow for more efficient and effective fine-tuning of diffusion models, potentially leading to state-of-the-art results in various tasks. However, the added complexity may lead to increased training time or decreased stability in large-scale settings.

TITLE: Theory of KL-Regularization for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We provide a theoretical analysis of the impact of KL-regularization on the fine-tuning of diffusion models. We derive a bound on the optimal reward achievable by the fine-tuned model, in terms of the KL divergence between the pre-trained and fine-tuned models' distributions. We also establish conditions under which the KL-regularization ensures convergence to a stable solution, and investigate the relationship between the regularization strength and the rate of convergence.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Efficient KL Regularization for Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: We will experiment with a tiled KL divergence regulation strategy for diffusion models, where instead of regulating the KL divergence with respect to the learned reverse process, we regulate with respect to multiple intermediate processes sampled around the original one, similar to ensemble methods for uncertainty estimation in Monte Carlo methods. This will allow us to learn a more robust "reference" distribution that better captures the pre-trained model's features. We will test this on the text-to-image generation task using the DALL-E model and the IAM Dataset of Document Image Layout Analysis. Additionally, we will compare against the standard KL-regularized PPO and a variant that reduces the KL term's impact, replacing it with a penalty on the marginal likelihood of the intermediate samples.
CONTROLS: PPO with standard KL regularization, PPO with reduced KL regularization, a baseline model trained without fine-tuning.
COST: 332.5
PREDICTION: We expect the "tiled" KL regulation strategy to offer stable and effective fine-tuning, reducing the initial value function bias problem.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Leveraging Denoising Trajectory Structure in Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We will analyze the structure of denoising trajectories in diffusion models and design experiments to expose how leveraging this structure can improve fine-tuning. We'll investigate whether segmenting the denoising process into intermediate "prior" and "posterior" steps, and learning separate models or regularizers for them, can reduce the difficulty of fine-tuning and improve results. We will apply this to the document layout generation task using the DALL-E model and the IAM Layout Dataset, comparing our approach to the standard KL-regularized PPO and the "tiled" KL regulation strategy from proposal 1.
CONTROLS: standard KL-regularized PPO, "tiled" KL regulation strategy, ablation experiments for the segmenting step.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: We expect that leveraging the denoising trajectory structure can lead to significant improvements in fine-tuning performance, particularly in tasks where the structural complexity of the data allows for clear separation of the prior and posterior steps.

PROPOSAL: We will investigate the possibility of correcting errors in pre-trained flow models without using explicit reward functions. We will explore retrospectively studying the causes of errors by analyzing the differences between generated samples and actual data, and then develop algorithms to learn corrections based on these differences. We'll test this approach on the document layout generation task using the DALL-E model and the IAM Layout Dataset.

PREDICTION: We expect that the proposed approach will enable correction of errors in pre-trained flow models without relying on explicit reward functions, leading to improved sample quality and potentially enabling applications where only unlabelled data is available.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Connection Between Best-of-N Sampling and KL-Regularized Reward Maximization
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the theoretical connection between Best-of-N sampling (a type of rejection sampling) and KL-regularized reward maximization for diffusion models. Specifically, we will prove that, in certain cases, Best-of-N sampling can be seen as equivalent to optimizing a KL-regularized objective. We will derive this connection using information-theoretic arguments and study its implications for understanding the behavior of different finetuning algorithms.
CONTROLS: None (theoretical investigation)
COST: 537.0859
PREDICTION: We expect that our theoretical connection will provide new insights into the relationships between various finetuning algorithms, and help in understanding the effective regularization mechanisms at play in Best-of-N sampling.

PROPOSAL: We propose an experiment fine-tuning a pre-trained diffusion model using a KL-regularized reward maximization objective with a synthetic trajectory KL divergence upper bound, evaluated on text-to-image generation tasks using the DALL-E 2 dataset. We evaluate our results using the Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) metric and compare with the KL-free baseline using the original PPO algorithm.

TITLE: Leveraging the Generative Structure of Diffusion Models for Efficient KL-Regularization
PROPOSAL: We propose an experiment exploring the use of the generative structure of diffusion models to efficiently compute the KL divergence between the fine-tuned distribution and the reference model distribution. Specifically, we propose a method to split the KL divergence into a sum of local KL divergences between intermediate noisy states and the reference model, and use this decomposition to derive an approximate KL regularization term that can be computed using standard forward passes. This experiment evaluates the effectiveness of this approach on fine-tuning diffusion models for molecule generation using the ZINC dataset and text-to-image generation tasks using the DALL-E 2 dataset.
CONTROLS: We compare our proposed method against the standard KL-regularized reward maximization objective and against an oracle baseline that uses the exact KL divergence for regularization. Additionally, we ablate different ways to compute the local KL divergences and their regularization terms.
COST: 2812.5
PREDICTION: We expect our proposed method to significantly speed up the computation of the KL regularization term and lead to faster convergence rates, but may require careful tuning of hyperparameters to achieve optimal results.

PROPOSAL: Conduct a mixed-methods analysis of the impact of RMS normalization on activation steering using a set of state-of-the-art LLMs on the CLINC OOS dataset. We will compare the efficacy of steering operations with and without normalization, utilizing metrics such as model fluency, factuality, and behavior control.

TITLE: A Differentiable Steering Primitive for LLMs
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel steering primitive, "contour editing", which smoothly modifies a target behavior by adjusting the input activations using a differentiable contour manipulation operation on the activation space (e.g., alpha-blend and boundary-adjust). This approach takes advantage of the readout-hold component that can be used to progressively scale activations during inference in transformer models. We will investigate its efficacy on steering behaviors for refusal of harmful requests on the amass dataset and the coherence and diverse outputs on the ROCStories dataset.
CONTROLS: Compare against the widely used activation addition and directional ablation primitives, as well as a baseline model with no steering operations.

PREDICTION: We expect to achieve more soft control over the target behavior with contour editing, reducing the brittleness observed in previous steering operations, but the new primitive should not surpass the ease of tuning of add for particular settings. The scalability of the method could fail for complex models with dense and numerous hidden state.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Activation Steering with Layer-Invariant Control Parameters
PROPOSAL: Design and evaluate a layer-invariant control parameter for activation steering, comprising a learned embedding that generalizes across layers and captures the orthogonal subspace of target behaviors. To this end, we propose to learn a small set of layer-invariant embeddings using our desired behavior label and its orthogonal counterpart learned via contrastive learning. We will then evaluate the effectiveness of these control parameters on a range of tasks, focusing on model families of different sizes and styles.
CONTROLS: Compare against state-of-the-art activation addition and ablation methods via experiments on revealing-to-releasing language modeling and emotion control in generated text
COST: 3325
PREDICTION: Our method outperforms existing activation steering approaches in terms of its ability to provide continuous, fine-grained control over target behaviors, but performance may degrade for extremely low- or high-control settings.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Understanding Activation Steering in Normalized Activation Space
PROPOSAL: Investigate how RMS normalization affects the existing activation steering operations (activation addition and ablation) and derive their effects in the normalized space. We will decompose the steering operations into components that are either orthogonal or parallel to the normalized activation direction. This decomposition will provide insights into the behavior of activation steering in activation spaces that have been normalized before processing.
CONTROLS: Compare against the original steering operations without layer normalization
COST: 5000
PREDICTION: The decomposition reveals that normalization mainly affects the strength of the steering effects, leading to activation addition being less sensitive to its coefficient and ablation potentially causing bigger abrupt changes in model outputs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Continuity of Steering Effects across Control Parameter Values
PROPOSAL: Conduct an in-depth analysis of how model behavior changes as the steering strength varies continuously for both activation addition and ablation in normalized activation space. We will explore scenarios where the model is manipulated to refuse vs. comply with a harmful request, examining whether gradual changes in control parameter values result in smooth, coherent outputs. To quantify this, we will use metrics such as coherence and consistency.
CONTROLS: Compare against a baseline that uses randomly sampled control parameters and an ablation study of the steering operations

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Continuously Adjustable Activation Steering with Spatial Gates
PROPOSAL: We extend directional ablation with a spatial gate modulating ablation strength in each layer, controlled by a learnable, activation-dependent weight. The gate would learn to adaptively scale the ablation strength for each steering feature, based on the layer-specific context, so that steering can accommodate mandatory differences between layer norms without hyperparameter tuning.
CONTROLS: Compare our method against directional ablation with fixed coefficients, varied ablation thresholds, and ablation orthogonalized at each layer separately.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our method allows more flexible activation adjustments, potentially leading to smoother behavior changes and better separation between steering directions, but its performance may hinge on the gate's learnability, particularly in deeper models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Incorporating Activation Rescaling Effects from Normalization Layers
PROPOSAL: We simulate the impact of RMS normalization throughout the LLM's depth using synthetic activations and analyze how steering operations behave under rescaling, as opposed to the original activation vectors. We investigate whether rescaling largely eclipses or complements the ablation and addition effects and assess how our spatial gate from Proposal 1 adjusts under these conditions. Additionally, we explore how leading spatial gates can be trained to explicitly account for rescaling artifacts, addressing their influence in real-world applications.
CONTROLS: Compare our method to ablation and addition without rescaling compensation, and exchange rescaling models (e.g. LARS, batch norm) to examine these dynamics in distinct dominant activation regulators.
COST: 270 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Understanding rescaling's effects might allow more informed steering decision-making and shed light on why superseding traditional parameter tuning may not unlock better synthesis overall.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Verifying Activation Steerability using Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: We extend the existing contrastive learning framework for behavior induction and suppression by including a feature-based contrastive loss term, which measures the steerability of the activation space along a specific direction. This allows us to quantify the degree to which a model's behavior can be controlled using activation steering, and identify the most controllable behaviors in a given model.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of our steerability estimator against traditional citation metrics, such as engagement metrics, and explore its relationship with the spatial gates from Proposal 1.
COST: 1080 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This method could provide a useful tool for verifying the effectiveness of activation steering for specific behaviors and identifying potential weaknesses in existing model control methods, but may require careful tuning of hyperparameters to achieve reliable results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Continuously Adjustable Coefficients for Activation Addition
PROPOSAL: We investigate the use of continuously adjustable coefficients for the activation addition technique, aiming to overcome the limitations of discrete hyperparameter search and provide fine-grained control over the strength of the behavior-modulating signal. Specifically, we explore techniques for learning or adapting coefficients in an online or incremental manner, allowing for behavior control in real-time as the model processes input sequences.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of fixed and adaptive coefficients for activation addition on a range of real-world datasets (e.g., the Toxic Comment Classification dataset and a dataset evaluating emotional control of generated text).
COST: 9800
PREDICTION: The use of continuously adjustable coefficients could lead to improvements in coherence and accuracy, especially in scenarios where precise control over behavior is necessary. However, we also expect to encounter challenges in stabilizing the coefficient updates, particularly for longer input sequences, and the need to address self-reinforcing biases or feedback loops that might complicate adaptive steering.

TITLE: End-to-End Differentiable Behavior Regulation via Meta-Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose an end-to-end differentiable behavior regulation framework that integrates activation steering into a meta-learning framework, allowing for simultaneous optimization of behavior and model parameters. This enables the model to learn a sensorimotor policy that adapts to new situations and tasks, while maintaining control over its behavior. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach on a range of tasks, including refusal of harmful requests and emotion control of generated text.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of our end-to-end differentiable behavior regulation framework with traditional activation steering techniques, as well as baseline models (e.g., vanilla transformer-based LLMs) on a selection of real-world datasets.
COST: 12165
PREDICTION: The use of meta-learning could enable models to generalize behavior control across a range of tasks and situations, but may require careful balancing of behavior regulation and model optimization objective functions, as well as techniques for stabilizing optimization and preventing catastrophic forgetting.

TITLE: Continuously Adjustable Coefficients for Activation Addition
PROPOSAL: We investigate the use of continuously adjustable coefficients for the activation addition technique, aiming to overcome the limitations of discrete hyperparameter search and provide fine-grained control over the strength of the behavior-modulating signal. Specifically, we explore techniques for learning or adapting coefficients in an online or incremental manner, allowing for behavior control in real-time as the model processes input sequences.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of fixed and adaptive coefficients for activation addition on a range of real-world datasets (e.g., the Toxic Comment Classification dataset and a dataset evaluating emotional control of generated text).

However, we also expect to encounter challenges in stabilizing the coefficient updates, particularly for longer input sequences, and the need to address self-reinforcing biases or feedback loops that might complicate adaptive steering.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: End-to-End Differentiable Behavior Regulation via Meta-Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose an end-to-end differentiable behavior regulation framework that integrates activation steering into a meta-learning framework, allowing for simultaneous optimization of behavior and model parameters. This enables the model to learn a sensorimotor policy that adapts to new situations and tasks, while maintaining control over its behavior. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach on a range of tasks, including refusal of harmful requests and emotion control of generated text.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of our end-to-end differentiable behavior regulation framework with traditional activation steering techniques, as well as baseline models (e.g., vanilla transformer-based LLMs) on a selection of real-world datasets.
COST: 36480
PREDICTION: The use of meta-learning could enable models to generalize behavior control across a range of tasks and situations, but may require careful balancing of behavior regulation and model optimization objective functions, as well as techniques for stabilizing optimization and preventing catastrophic forgetting.

PROPOSAL: We revise our approach for continuously adjustable coefficients for activation addition to include an explicit exploration-exploitation trade-off, allowing the model to adapt the coefficient values in a more informed and efficient manner. Specifically, we will use a entropy-regularized coefficient updating mechanism, which encourages the model to explore a range of coefficient values while still exploiting the best-performing values. This should improve the stability and robustness of the model when adapting to new input sequences or tasks.
CONTROLS: We will compare the effectiveness of the revised coefficient updating mechanism with the original approach, as well as baseline models without adaptive coefficient tuning.
COST: 40320
PREDICTION: The addition of an exploration-exploitation trade-off should improve the coefficient updating mechanism, but may require careful tuning of the hyperparameters controlling the trade-off. We expect to see improved stability and robustness in the model's behavior, particularly in challenging scenarios where precise control is necessary. However, we may also encounter challenges in balancing exploration and exploitation, and ensuring that the model doesn't over-exploit or under-explore the coefficient space.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Representation Alignment with a Heterogeneous Graph
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel graph-based method for aligning representations produced by an arbitrary number of models, under the assumption that each user's local model can be represented as a node in a graph, and edges between nodes correspond to the semantic relationships between tasks or architectures. The graph can be inferred from a pre-training dataset or constructed based on prior knowledge. Users' models are then adapted to fit the learned graph structure, enabling effective joint alignment of their representations.
CONTROLS: Compare against the recently proposed Gramian-based contrastive loss and establish baselines with a naive graph-based method that only considers direct nearest neighbors.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: We anticipate the graph-based approach to be more effective in capturing the dependencies among all models, particularly in cases where there are intricate relationships between tasks. However, the graph inference step might be computationally expensive, and the method's convergence could be sensitive to the quality of the graph.

(Note: our implementation will consider also UMAP, PCA for each task for the recorded embeddings to infer the Graph structure using GNN's)

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Heterogeneous Federated Multi-Task Learning via Task-Agnostic Projection
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel federated multi-task learning method that enables collaboration among users with heterogeneous model architectures and different tasks. The approach involves learning a task-agnostic projection matrix that aligns the representations of all users in a shared representation space. Each user trains a local model, and we use a variant of the InfoNCE loss to update the projection matrix in a decentralized manner. We align the user representations using the learned projection matrix and optimize the model parameters and the projection matrix simultaneously.
CONTROLS: We compare our method with recent state-of-the-art methods for heterogeneous federated multi-task learning, including a knowledge-distillation-based approach and a method that adds a proximal term based on centered kernel alignment. We also evaluate the performance of our method on real-world datasets and benchmark it against a baseline that trains each user's model independently.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: Our method should outperform the baselines by a significant margin due to its ability to capture the dependencies among the representations obtained from all users. However, its performance may degrade in scenarios where the task-agnostic projection matrix is not able to capture the underlying relationships between tasks.

Turn 2 will build on this proposal by identifying some promising datasets and real-world benchmarks.

TITLE: Model-Agnostic Multi-Task Meta-Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose a model-agnostic multi-task meta-learning framework, where each user's model is treated as a task-specific learner, and the server aggregates task-agnostic information from multiple users using a meta-learner. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Federated Multi-Task Learning via Adaptive Knowledge Distillation
PROPOSAL: We will investigate a new federated multi-task learning framework that adapts knowledge distillation to accommodate users with heterogeneous model architectures and different tasks. The server will collect task-aligned outputs from users and use a dynamic ensemble method to compute a weighted average of the outputs, which serves as the pseudo-label for theHU KS or decoding step of aninova objective They provide more informations about unsupervised and semi-supervised learning via the objective function than let the users finetune. The weighted average will be computed based on the similarity between the task-specific predictors of different users, ensuring that users with more similar tasks contribute more to the pseudo-label. Each user will then fine-tune their model on the pseudo-labeled dataset generated by the server. We will evaluate the effectiveness of our framework on several real-world benchmarks, including federated learning tasks, and compare its performance with state-of-the-art methods.
CONTROLS: We will compare our framework with recent methods that use ensemble methods to adapt knowledge distillation, such as Multi-KL and FED-VIA, as well as with methods that assume model congruity, such as FED-MT. We will also investigate the importance of the weighted average step by comparing our framework with a variant that uses a simple mean ensemble method.
COST: 332.5
PREDICTION: Our framework should outperform existing methods in terms of task accuracy and model generalization, especially in scenarios with heterogeneous model architectures and tasks. However, it may require significant computational resources to compute the weighted average, which could lead to communication constraints in practical deployments.

TITLE: Federated Multi-Task Learning via Adaptive Knowledge Distillation with Error Correction
PROPOSAL: We will revise our previous proposal (Federated Multi-Task Learning via Adaptive Knowledge Distillation) by incorporating an error correction mechanism to improve the pseudo-labeling process. Specifically, we will use a technique called active learning to select a subset of users and re-run the knowledge distillation process to correct any errors in the pseudo-labels. This will allow the server to iteratively refine the pseudo-labels and improve the accuracy of the final models. We will also explore different error correction strategies, such as re-weighting the loss function to give more importance to misclassified samples.
CONTROLS: We will compare our revised method with the original Adaptive Knowledge Distillation method, as well as with other state-of-the-art methods that use ensemble methods to adapt knowledge distillation, such as Multi-KL and FED-VIA.
COST: 36000
PREDICTION: Our revised method should lead to significant improvements in model accuracy, especially in scenarios with noisy or imbalanced data. However, we may need to carefully tune the error correction mechanism to avoid over-correction.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Federated Learning for Multi-Task Alignment
PROPOSAL: We will propose a hierarchical federated learning framework for multi-task alignment, which consists of two levels: a global level where the server aggregates the knowledge from users and a local level where users fine-tune their models on the aggregated knowledge. At the global level, we will use a multi-task learning framework to align the representations across users using the knowledge distillation approach. At the local level, we will use a Federated Averaging approach to fine-tune the user models on the aggregated knowledge. We will also introduce a novel hierarchical loss function to combine the global and local loss functions and update the user models accordingly.
CONTROLS: We will compare our method with recent methods that use hierarchical federated learning, such as FedAI and Hierarchical FedAvg, as well as with other state-of-the-art methods that use knowledge distillation and multi-task learning.
COST: 5000
PREDICTION: Our method should lead to more effective alignment of representations across users, especially in scenarios with diverse model architectures and learning objectives, while also being able to handle hierarchical knowledge aggregation and local fine-tuning. However, we may need to carefully tune the hierarchical loss function to ensure optimal performance.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Efficient Federated Contrastive Learning for Multi-Task Alignment with Split-Batch Training
PROPOSAL: We will revisit our previous proposal (Efficient Federated Contrastive Learning for Multi-Task Alignment) and adapt it to use split-batch training to further reduce the communication overhead. In split-batch training, the server divides the data into multiple batches and sends them to the users to train on. We will modify the Gramian-based contrastive loss to account for the split-batch training framework and propose an efficient gradient aggregation algorithm to handle the gradients from multiple batches. This will enable the server to efficiently align the representations across users while reducing the communication overhead.
CONTROLS: We will compare our revised method with the original Efficient Federated Contrastive Learning method, as well as with other state-of-the-art methods that use split-batch training, such as SplitFed and FedSplit.
COST: 6000
PREDICTION: Our revised method should lead to significant reductions in communication overhead and improved alignment of representations across users. However, we may need to carefully tune the split-batch training parameters to ensure optimal performance.

TITLE: Federated Learning with Multi-Task Private-Sum Aggregation
PROPOSAL: We will propose a new federated learning framework that combines multi-task learning with private-sum aggregation to align the representations across users while protecting the user data. In private-sum aggregation, the server aggregates the gradients from users in a way that preserves the user's privacy. We will extend private-sum aggregation to multi-task learning by aggregating the gradients from users across multiple tasks and using a novel aggregation strategy to align the representations across tasks. We will evaluate our method on several real-world benchmarks and compare its performance with state-of-the-art methods.
CONTROLS: We will compare our method with recent methods that use private-sum aggregation and multi-task learning, such as DP-FedAvg and Multi-Task FedAvg.
COST: 6720
PREDICTION: Our method should lead to improved alignment of representations across users while preserving the user's privacy. However, we may need to carefully tune the aggregation strategy to ensure optimal performance.

TITLE: Federated Multi-Task Learning via Adaptive Knowledge Distillation
PROPOSAL: We will investigate a new federated multi-task learning framework that adapts knowledge distillation to accommodate users with heterogeneous model architectures and different tasks. The server will collect task-aligned outputs from users and use a dynamic ensemble method to compute a weighted average of the outputs, which serves as the pseudo-label for theHU KS or decoding step of aninova objective They provide more informations about unsupervised and semi-supervised learning via the objective function than let the users finetune. The weighted average will be computed based on the similarity between the task-specific predictors of different users, ensuring that users with more similar tasks contribute more to the pseudo-label. Each user will then fine-tune their model on the pseudo-labeled dataset generated by the server. We will evaluate the effectiveness of our framework on several real-world benchmarks, including federated learning tasks, and compare its performance with state-of-the-art methods.
CONTROLS: We will compare our framework with recent methods that use ensemble methods to adapt knowledge distillation, such as Multi-KL and FED-VIA, as well as with methods that assume model congruity, such as FED-MT. We will also investigate the importance of the weighted average step by comparing our framework with a variant that uses a simple mean ensemble method.

However, it may require significant computational resources to compute the weighted average, which could lead to communication constraints in practical deployments.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Assessing Instance-Dependent Label Noise in Multi-Task Learning Benchmark
PROPOSAL: Train the extensively-used multiple-task learning benchmark Diverse Datasets for Benchmarking (D2B) suite with 3 different levels of instance-dependent label noise, including "{+}", "{-}", and "{*: ix-ix jitter}", to assess its sensitivity to noisy labels in three real-world domains (natural image classification, disease diagnosis from medical images, and text classification).
CONTROLS: Train on the D2B suite with clean labels as a baseline; also train with a class-conditional noise distribution model as a comparison point.
COST: 1500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see worsening performance and an increase in noise levels with increased instance-dependent label noise; failure could be observed if the watermark present inside model's weights used to generate the noisy labels leaks into the results.

PROPOSAL: Implement and compare the performance of three active learning strategies (query-by-committee, uncertainty sampling, and human-in-the-loop) with a fixed pool size of 10% on four datasets (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet and -scale 14 paired ADNI dataset, in DSP task extraction and individual questionnable voxel error), with and without label noise to see how active learning improves robustness.

PROPOSAL: Implement a novel self-training method, dual-warmup learning, that learns a correction model to correct the noisy labels and trains a prediction model on the corrected data. TITLE: Confidence-Weighted Training with Multiple Noise Estimators
PROPOSAL: Design a method that combines multiple noise estimators and selectively weights the training samples based on their predicted noise probabilities and model confidence levels. PREDICTION: The proposed method outperforms baselines by selectively leveraging the reliability of noise estimators and model confidence, showing improved robustness against instance-dependent label noise. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial Label Defense with Ensembles and Activated Tracing
PROPOSAL: Develop an adversarial label defense method that leverages an ensemble of models and activated tracing to detect and correct label noise. In this method, the models in the ensemble are forced to disagree on the correct labels through activated tracing, which identifies the misleading labels and creates a confidence profile for each sample. This confidence profile is used as a guide to reweight the loss function during training, promoting the learning of correct labels and discriminating against noisy ones.
CONTROLS: Baselines include standard classifier trained on clean labels, standard classifier trained on noisy labels with vanilla reweighting, and a state-of-the-art adversarial training method for label noise.
COST: 160 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed method demonstrates significant improvement in defense against instance-dependent label noise by effectively leveraging the diversity of ensemble models and correcting the misleading labels. However, it may be computationally expensive and may require careful hyperparameter tuning.

TITLE: Investigating Enhanced Label Correction Strategies
PROPOSAL:  Experimentally evaluate the efficacy of three enhanced label correction strategies on the clothing1M, WebVision, and Stanford Cars datasets: (1) BoostCorreg: a revised version of BoostNet in which correction probabilities are dynamically adjusted based on instance-dependent noise levels estimated during training, (2) CoCorrect: a combination of consistency regularization and correction weighting, where clean labels are selectively amplified during training in proportion to the true prediction confidence, and (3) EpochILogReg: a method that iteratively refines the correction model, leveraging detailed information about the prediction performance of the training class probabilities.
CONTROLS: Baselines: standard train-test split, purely noisy, and noise-free setups; ablations: using each label correction strategy in isolation; and three noise levels: 10%, 20%, and 50% for each dataset.
COST: 3,110.4 GPU-hours

PREDICTION: The proposed methods, especially BoostCorreg and EpochILogReg, are expected to outperform standard training on real-world datasets, especially under increased noise levels. However, their increased complexity may lead to potential overfitting issues.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Theoretical Analysis of Label Noising
PROPOSAL:  Theoretical analysis of label noising for a simple linear classifier in the noise-free regime. We prove that the risk of a label-noised classifier can be bounded by the corresponding risk of a clean classifier, using the concept of "Risk in expectation". This relates the noise distribution to the capacity of the learning model, with implications for how well a model will generalize when trained on noisy data.
CONTROLS: Theoretical: assuming standard noise models, analytic risk bounds, and proofs of convergence using Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and triangle inequality.
COST: 7,200 GPU-hours

PREDICTION: The risk bound established will provide insights into designing models or algorithms that are more tolerant to noisy labels, restricting failures to cases with extremely high noise levels or complex learning structures.

TITLE: Theoretical Analysis of Label Noising
PROPOSAL:  Theoretical analysis of label noising for a simple linear classifier in the noise-free regime. We prove that the risk of a label-noised classifier can be bounded by the corresponding risk of a clean classifier, using the concept of "Risk in expectation". This relates the noise distribution to the capacity of the learning model, with implications for how well a model will generalize when trained on noisy data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: RGB-Event Fusion for High-Frame-Rate Semantic Perception
PROPOSAL: We compare the performance of four fusion methods on the KITTI dataset: (1) Spatial Attention Network [1], which learns to weigh event and RGB features; (2) Channel Attention Network [2], which attends to relevant channels in both modalities; (3) Depth-wise Separable Transform [3], which learns a spatially-varying transformation matrix; and (4) our novel contribution, a Cycle-Consistent Fusion (CCF) module. CCF aligns RGB and event features using an autoencoder, enabling semantic information in the RGB image to be synchronized with the event stream, while suppressing irrelevant noise in both modalities. We train all models using Cross-Entropy loss and evaluate them on the KITTI semantic segmentation validation set.
CONTROLS: We compare these fusion methods against state-of-the-art video semantic segmentation methods: PSPNet [4], ResNeSt [5], and the frame-wise baseline, DeeplabV3+ [6].
COST: 19200
PREDICTION: We expect CCF to outperform the other methods, achieving mean IoU > 85%, while being robust to dynamic scenes and occlusions. Failure risk: (1) method generalizability when faced with diverse real-world scenarios; (2) potential overfitting to the KITTI dataset, impacting transfer to other domains.

We add a new loss term to the CCF framework that rewards sub-stream predictions (intermediate predictions in the per-pixel temporal dimension) exhibiting low temporal variability. The new loss function becomes a weighted sum of the original CCF loss and the TR loss, which is calculated using the temporal variance of sub-stream predictions. This regularization term enables the model to learn a more temporally coherent and less oscillatory trajectory of predictions, reflecting the spatial structure of events more accurately.

PROPOSAL: Introduce a counterfactual event inpainting approach to address temporally incomplete scenes by leveraging the event stream to create plausible semantic completions of missing events. TITLE: Event-Driven High-Frame-Rate Semantic Segmentation via Multi-Task Learning
PROPOSAL: Train a multi-task learning model that jointly predicts a dense semantic segmentation map at the target time $t+\delta t$ and an event-driven semantic map at the generating time of each event, given the initial RGB frame $I_t$ and the corresponding event stream $\mathcal{E}_{t-\Delta t \to t+\delta t}$. Use two identical encoder-decoder architectures with different outputs for the semantic segmentation and event-driven semantic maps, share the encoder's output between the two tasks, and jointly train both segments using a combination of their respective losses (e.g., cross-entropy and masked mean absolute error).
CONTROLS: Use the same multi-task learning model without event-driven loss for a baseline evaluation, and further ablate the coupling of tasks by removing shared layers.
COST: 500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This method should yield state-of-the-art results in predicting dense semantic maps for all offsets $\delta t$, while maintaining real-time processing for practical application. However, the increased computational cost might pose a challenge in the low-frame-rate scenarios.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: "Transient Event-RGB Fusion for High-Frame-Rate Semantic Perception"
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel event-RGB fusion approach called "Hrung NRQLoRo" that leverages a specifically designed neural network architecture to combine the spatial and temporal information from RGB frames and event streams. This architecture will consist of a preliminary event>Noise reduction module NoizeCap QLo, an adaptive gating mechanism to dynamically integrate event information into the RGB semantic map, and a localized feature uncertainty regulation Neural loop LRLo for enhancing spatial coherence. 
The final dense semantic prediction at any target time $t + \delta t$ is generated through a cutting-edge S-FewArcS semantic segmentation module. 
We aim to demonstrate that our method produces accurate and dense semantic predictions despite the temporal and spatial information disparities between RGB and event streams.
CTRLS: This proposal will be evaluated using existing eventsemantic benchmarks (e.g. the ETH-EDUB dataset and the Stanford Event Camera Dataset) and compared to our selfdeveloped eventdog video S-Semseg, which leverages ground truth events from known setups to establish synchronous RGBevent pairs for evaluation.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Our method will outperform current state-of-the-art fusion techniques in accuracy, with minor loss of efficiency, in real-world high-speed autonomous driving and drone navigation environments.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: "Improving Temporal Consistency in Event-RGB Fusion using Physics-aware Latent Space"
PROPOSAL: This supplementary task aims to enhance the temporal consistency of our `Hung NRQLoRo` approach by incorporating physics-aware latent space constraints in the event-RGB fusion process. Specifically, we develop and integrate a mechanism called `tmp_pwIFIppiT`, which captures the physical dynamics of objects and uses this knowledge to refine the event-RGB fusion at the latent feature level. This ensures that the produced semantic maps better respect temporal coherence and adhere to the real-world physical constraints.
CTRLS: This proposal will be compared to an ablated version of `Hung NRQLoRo` without the `tmp_pwIFIppiT` mechanism, and intersecting methods that integrate physics information such as the `scenesAsync broad`.
COST: 690 
PREDICTION: Our physics-aware modification significantly improves the temporal consistency of the generated semantic maps, effectively reducing the appearance of artifacts in dynamic scenes such as those from our validation images from real-world quadruped robot navigation tests.

PROPOSAL: We propose a comprehensive real-world validation and benchmarking framework to evaluate the performance of our event-RGB fusion approaches on autonomous driving, drone navigation, and quadruped robot navigation applications. This framework, called "RealTESTing", leverages existing real-world datasets (e.g., KITTI, UCAS, and its association successor) and widely adopted evaluation metrics (e.g., intersection over union, accuracy) to provide a robust assessment of the methods.

The framework will serve as a baseline for future research in high-frame-rate semantic perception.

TITLE: Unsupervised Auto-Encoder Objective for Personalized 3D Generation
PROPOSAL: Introduce an unsupervised auto-encoder objective where the generator is trained to encode input 2D data (image/video) into a compact 3D latent representation that can be decoded back into novel views. Include a regularization term that encourages the generator to encode subjectspecific appearance features.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed unsupervised objective against a supervised objective that learns to predict novel views directly from the input data. Also, pre-train the generator using standard 3D generation objectives and fine-tune it using the proposed unsupervised objective to examine the benefits of transfer learning.
COST: 2400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This method will demonstrate decent results on subjects with simple topologies, but its performance may degrade for complex subjects with intricate features. 

(This assumes that training an auto-encoder, followed by fine-tuning using transfer learning, will require some significant compute power, likely around 2000-3000 GPU-hours.)

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Improving Personalization in 3D/4D Generation with Virtual View Synthesis
PROPOSAL: We'll leverage recent advancements in image-to-image translation and virtual view synthesis (VVS) to develop a VVS-based 3D/4D generator that synthesizes novel views of a subject from a given single reference image or video, and uses them as multi-view observations to inform the generation of a personalized 3D/4D asset.
CONTROLS: We will compare our VVS-based approach to a baseline that uses a standard multi-view diffusion model for hallucinating novel views, and ablate to verify the contribution of the VVS component to the quality of the generated designs.
COST: 16.56 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect improved subject-driven 3D/4D generation quality, reduced hallucination, and enhanced preservation of the subject's identity across viewpoints, but may struggle to accurately preserve fine details and high-frequency textures in certain regions (e.g., fur, hair).

TITLE: Exploring Identity-Aware Optimization for Personalized 3D/4D Generation
PROPOSAL: Building on recent works on identity-aware optimization, we'll develop an optimization strategy that incorporates identity-preserving losses to fine-tune a multi-view generation model on a small dataset of a specific subject, with the goal of generating a personalized 3D/4D asset that accurately preserves the subject's identity.
CONTROLS: We will compare our identity-aware optimization approach to standard finetuning and ablate to study the impact of different identity-preserving losses on the quality of the generated designs, as well as their sensitivity to the choice of reference image or video and the size of the fine-tuning dataset.

CONTROLS: We will evaluate the performance of transfer learning approaches using a set of tasks involving genre, species, and domain shifts, and will compare the results to a baseline that uses only self-supervised finetuning.
COST: 367.5 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to demonstrate the efficacy of transfer learning in reducing the sample complexity of personalized 3D/4D generation, and to identify key factors that influence the success of transfer learning in different domains.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Improving Personalization in 3D/4D Generation with Virtual View Synthesis
PROPOSAL: We'll leverage recent advancements in image-to-image translation and virtual view synthesis (VVS) to develop a VVS-based 3D/4D generator that synthesizes novel views of a subject from a given single reference image or video, and uses them as multi-view observations to inform the generation of a personalized 3D/4D asset.
CONTROLS: We will compare our VVS-based approach to a baseline that uses a standard multi-view diffusion model for hallucinating novel views, and ablate to verify the contribution of the VVS component to the quality of the generated designs.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect improved subject-driven 3D/4D generation quality, reduced hallucination, and enhanced preservation of the subject's identity across viewpoints, but may struggle to accurately preserve fine details and high-frequency textures in certain regions (e.g., fur, hair).

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Identity-Aware Optimization for Personalized 3D/4D Generation
PROPOSAL: Building on recent works on identity-aware optimization, we'll develop an optimization strategy that incorporates identity-preserving losses to fine-tune a multi-view generation model on a small dataset of a specific subject, with the goal of generating a personalized 3D/4D asset that accurately preserves the subject's identity.
CONTROLS: We will compare our identity-aware optimization approach to standard finetuning and ablate to study the impact of different identity-preserving losses on the quality of the generated designs, as well as their sensitivity to the choice of reference image or video and the size of the fine-tuning dataset.
COST: 320 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect improved identity preservation, reduced hallucination, and enhanced personalization quality, but may face challenges in adapting the identity-aware optimization to subjects with complex or highly variable appearances.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Exploring Identity-Aware Optimization for Personalized 3D/4D Generation
PROPOSAL: Building on recent works on identity-aware optimization, we'll develop an optimization strategy that incorporates identity-preserving losses to fine-tune a multi-view generation model on a small dataset of a specific subject, and will specifically investigate the use of style-based discriminators and image-to-image translation losses to preserve the subject's identity.
CONTROLS: We will compare our revised identity-aware optimization approach to standard finetuning, using a fine-tuning dataset curated from the ShapeNet dataset, and ablate to study the impact of different identity-preserving losses and style-based discriminators on the quality of the generated designs.
COST: 320 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect improved identity preservation and reduced hallucination, and will investigate whether the use of style-based discriminators and image-to-image translation losses enhances the personalization quality of the generated designs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Personalized 3D/4D Generation using Hybrid Reconstruction and Optimization
PROPOSAL: We'll develop a hybrid approach that integrates multi-view image reconstruction with identity-aware optimization to generate personalized 3D/4D assets, leveraging the strengths of both techniques to achieve improved identity preservation and reduced hallucination.
CONTROLS: We will compare our hybrid approach to a baseline that uses only multi-view image reconstruction, and to an ablation where we remove the identity-aware optimization component.
COST: 800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect improved identity preservation, reduced hallucination, and enhanced personalization quality, but may face challenges in optimizing the trade-off between reconstruction and optimization, and in scaling the approach to large datasets.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Personalized 3D/4D Generation using Hybrid Reconstruction and Optimization
PROPOSAL: We'll develop a hybrid approach that integrates multi-view image reconstruction with identity-aware optimization and incorporates a novel 'feature transfer' mechanism to transfer the subject's identity from the reference image or video to the generated 3D/4D asset, leveraging a pre-trained VGG network to extract feature embeddings that are then transferred and refined during the optimization process.
CONTROLS: We will compare our revised hybrid approach to the baseline and ablation, and will also evaluate its performance on a variety of subjects with different appearance complexities and variability.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect significant improvements in identity preservation and reduced hallucination, and will investigate whether the feature transfer mechanism enhances the personalization quality of the generated designs.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Finetuning Image-2-3D Model with Multiple View Reconstructions
PROPOSAL: To improve the identity preservation of a state-of-the-art image-to-3D model, we will finetune it using a combination of multiple view reconstructions of the same scene. Specifically, we will adopt a four-view reconstruction setting, where three cameras capture front, side, and top views, and finetune the model using the rendering of these views. This setup will encourage the generator to learn a more consistent and subject-pose invariant 3D representation.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: No finetuning; Baseline 2: Finetuning with single-view reconstruction; Ablation study: Varying number of views used for finetuning.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By finetuning the model on multiple views, we expect to improve its ability to preserve identity across different viewpoints, with a potential drop in performance due to the increased complexity of the task. We hypothesize that a significant boost in performance will be observed when using three or four views for finetuning, while a single view may not be sufficient for effective identity preservation.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Diffusion-based View Inconsistency Loss for 3D Generation
PROPOSAL: To address the issue of view inconsistencies in 3D generation, we propose a novel loss term that measures the discrepancy between different views of a generated 3D asset. This loss term is based on a diffusion process, where the generator is encouraged to produce 3D assets that, when rendered from different angles, yield similar images. Specifically, we will use a variant of the Split-Resolution Diffusion model as the backbone for our 3D generation and incorporate a view inconsistency loss term that encourages consistent rendering across different views.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: No view inconsistency loss; Baseline 2: Using a traditional reconstruction loss (e.g. L1 or L2); Ablation study: Varying the strength of the view inconsistency loss.
COST: 180 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect this loss term to improve the consistency of generated 3D assets across different views, with a potential gain in performance when combined with the finetuning approach proposed in proposal 1. However, it may also lead to a decrease in texture detail or other aspects of the generated assets due to the additional loss term.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Real-world Validation on Personalized 3D Generation
PROPOSAL: To extend our proposed methods to real-world scenarios, we will conduct a small-scale experiment using a real-world dataset of images of various objects, including animals and people. We will select a subset of objects with sufficient view variability and conduct a manual evaluation of the generated 3D assets using both qualitative and quantitative metrics (e.g. Chamfer distance, MSE). This will help us to better understand how our methods generalize to real-world applications.
CONTROLS: Use the same baselines as in proposal 1 and 2, with additional real-world evaluation metrics and manual evaluation by human annotators.
COST: 40 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect our proposed methods to show promising results on real-world data, but the evaluation may be challenging due to the variability of real-world data and the difficulty of manual evaluation. We may observe a larger disconnect between synthetic and real-world results, and this could indicate additional challenges when adapting our methods to real-world scenarios.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Personalized 3D Generation using a Dual-Path Network
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel dual-path network architecture for personalized 3D generation, where one path is responsible for generating a coarsely rendered 3D asset and the other path refines it to produce the final output. The two paths are conditioned on the same input image, allowing the generator to capture both the global and local structural information of the object. Moreover, we will incorporate a regularization term to encourage the two paths to agree on the underlying 3D structure.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: Directly using a single 3D generation model; Baseline 2: Using a coarse-to-fine pipeline without the dual-path network; Ablation study: Varying the strength of the regularization term.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By leveraging the strengths of both coarse and fine 3D generation, we expect the dual-path network to improve the accuracy and richness of generated 3D assets. However, the additional complexity of the dual-path network may lead to increased computational requirements and overfitting, particularly in cases with limited training data.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Optimized Personalized 3D Generation using a Dual-Path Network
PROPOSAL: We refine the dual-path network proposal (4) by optimizing the architecture using a neural architecture search (NAS) technique. We will use a black-box optimization algorithm to search for the optimal combination of layers, cells, and channel numbers for the dual-path network. This will enable us to find a more efficient and effective architecture for personalized 3D generation.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: Using the conventional dual-path network architecture; Baseline 2: Using a pre-designed efficient network architecture; Ablation study: Varying the number of search iterations and the range of search space.
COST: 900 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By using NAS to optimize the dual-path network, we expect to find a more efficient and effective architecture for personalized 3D generation. However, the additional computational cost of NAS may lead to a longer training time and potential overfitting.
