However, the quality and realism of the synthesized data may vary depending on the specific generative models used, and the approach may require careful calibration to achieve optimal results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Marker Surrogate for Implicit Counterfactual Reasoning in Agentic Search
PROPOSAL: Introduce a surrogate learning framework that maps the agent's intermediate reasoning steps to markers of counterfactual outcomes, allowing us to implicitly evaluate the impact of different actions and hypotheses on the search trajectory. By learning to predict counterfactual outcomes, we can effectively test the robustness and reliability of the agent's reasoning and improve its ability to navigate complex search spaces.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the marker surrogate approach against a baseline that relies solely on contextualized intermediate rewards (proposed in proposal 1), as well as against a modified version of the Bayesian turn-level impurity minimization (revised in proposal 2), and against a baseline that doesn't use marker surrogate.
COST: 5670
PREDICTION: The marker surrogate approach should significantly improve the agent's ability to reason counterfactually and evaluate the impact of different actions, leading to more robust and reliable search results. However, the performance of the surrogate model may degrade in scenarios with highly nonlinear or complex relationships between the agent's actions and the search outcomes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Contextualized Intermediate Reward Engineering for Multi-Turn Search Agents
PROPOSAL: Experimenting with contextualized intermediate rewards derived from the ground-truth final answer and its surrounding context (e.g., query, question type, and supporting knowledge). The contextualized reward for each turn will be a weighted combination of three components: binary correctness, influence on the next turn (capturing the causal relationship between turns), and informativeness (how much new information is retrieved). We hypothesize that contextualized rewards will provide a dense, informative signal for RL training while staying anchored to the final task objective.
CONTROLS: We will compare our contextualized rewards (1) against outcome-only rewards ( baseline 1), (2) against random process rewards with similar sparsity (baseline 2), and (3) against ablated versions of our reward, where either the influence or informativeness component is removed.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: Contextualized rewards will improve sample efficiency and accuracy over baseline 1 (outcome-only reward) due to better credit assignment, especially in long trajectories. However, variance or bias from contextualized reward components might lead to suboptimal performance or instability in certain regimes, depending on the specific architecture and dataset.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Bayesian Turn-Level Impurity Minimization for Easier Credit Assignment
PROPOSAL: Introduce a Bayesian probabilistic model to mask the true ground-truth answer (or part of it) at each turn during training. The model will learn to predict the hidden information, enabling the agent to attend to relevant interactions and turn-level information without being prematurely biased toward the correct answer. This technique allows for turn-level supervision, focuses the agent's learning on critical steps, and may help alleviate credit assignment issues. An upper bound of the expected information gain after each turn will serve as our reward.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate our Bayesian turn-level model against the contextualized rewards (proposed in proposal 1) and compare it against a classic Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) baseline, evaluating the robustness of each method to hard or easy query difficulty, and varying the turn-level reward information gain.
COST: 4800
PREDICTION: The model should outperform the contextualized rewards, especially in challenging multi-hop questions or long trajectories where extraneous information clearly interferes with the final goal. It will, however, require more samples to be learned and evaluate, as accurate Bayesian inference is computationally more expensive.

PREDICTION: Turn-level soft outcome rewards will demonstrate lower variance and risk of collapse than standard outcome-only rewards, and maintain sample efficiency. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: AGM (Agentic Gradient Masking)
PROPOSAL: Introduce AGM, a masking mechanism that selectively filters out gradient signals from intermediate turns that are likely to lead to the final outcome. By reducing the influence of these turns on the overall policy update, AGM aims to prevent the advantage collapse and credit assignment issues present in outcome-only reward settings, without relying on dense process rewards or external supervision.
CONTROLS: AGM with turn-level soft outcome rewards, AGM without turn-level soft outcome rewards, standard GRPO with outcome-only rewards.
COST: 210
PREDICTION: AGM will show improved sample efficiency and reduced dependency on outcome-only rewards, but high levels of masking may lead to suboptimal policies due to loss of critical intermediate information.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Monitor-Modulated Group Relative Policy Optimization (MM-GRPO)
PROPOSAL: Introduce MM-GRPO, a modification of GRPO that adjusts the group relative advantage computation based on an explicit monitor signal indicative of the quality or coherence of intermediate reasoning or action steps. By using this monitor signal to up-weight rolls that follow more beneficial trajectories, MM-GRPO aims to provide informative rewards and mitigate the issues associated with outcome-only supervision.
CONTROLS: MM-GRPO with turn-level soft outcome rewards as monitor signal, GRPO with turn-level soft outcome rewards, standard GRPO with outcome-only rewards.
COST: 270
PREDICTION: MM-GRPO will demonstrate improved policy quality and more accurate credit assignment, but may introduce instability if the monitor signal is too strong or noisy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Intermediate Turn Filtering with Distillation
PROPOSAL: Introduce an intermediate turn filtering mechanism that utilizes a teacher-student distillation framework to identify and suppress unnecessary or suboptimal turns within a rollout. This framework will utilize a pre-trained robust model as a teacher that provides high-confidence preferences over the entire rollout, which will then be used to train a smaller student model to produce a sparse reward signal.
CONTROLS: Student-teacher distillation without filtering (Distilled Rewards), student-teacher distillation with filtering, standard GRPO with outcome-only rewards.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Intermediate Turn Filtering with Distillation will show improved sample efficiency and overall policy performance by eliminating non-informative turns and focusing the policy's attention on the most crucial steps, but may suffer from over-reliance on the teacher model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Turn-level Soft Outcome Rewards
PROPOSAL: Introduce turn-level soft outcome rewards, where each turn receives a reward that is a probability-normalized version of the ground-truth outcome reward. This normalization is done within each group of rollouts, but is turn-specific instead of outcome-specific. For example, if there are three turn-one rollouts and two turn-two rollouts that ultimately yield the correct answer, the probability-normalized reward for the first turn of the two already-correct rollouts would be higher than for the rollouts with incorrect intermediate steps.
CONTROLS: GRPO without soft outcome rewards, GRPO with standard outcome-only rewards.
COST: 270
PREDICTION: Turn-level soft outcome rewards will demonstrate lower variance and risk of collapse than standard outcome-only rewards, and maintain sample efficiency. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: AGM (Agentic Gradient Masking)
PROPOSAL: Introduce AGM, a masking mechanism that selectively filters out gradient signals from intermediate turns that are likely to lead to the final outcome. By reducing the influence of these turns on the overall policy update, AGM aims to prevent the advantage collapse and credit assignment issues present in outcome-only reward settings, without relying on dense process rewards or external supervision.
CONTROLS: AGM with turn-level soft outcome rewards, AGM without turn-level soft outcome rewards, standard GRPO with outcome-only rewards.
COST: 630
PREDICTION: AGM will show improved sample efficiency and reduced dependency on outcome-only rewards, but high levels of masking may lead to suboptimal policies due to loss of critical intermediate information.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Monitor-Modulated Group Relative Policy Optimization (MM-GRPO)
PROPOSAL: Introduce MM-GRPO, a modification of GRPO that adjusts the group relative advantage computation based on an explicit monitor signal indicative of the quality or coherence of intermediate reasoning or action steps. By using this monitor signal to up-weight rolls that follow more beneficial trajectories, MM-GRPO aims to provide informative rewards and mitigate the issues associated with outcome-only supervision.
CONTROLS: MM-GRPO with turn-level soft outcome rewards as monitor signal, GRPO with turn-level soft outcome rewards, standard GRPO with outcome-only rewards.
COST: 810
PREDICTION: MM-GRPO will demonstrate improved policy quality and more accurate credit assignment, but may introduce instability if the monitor signal is too strong or noisy.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Monitor-Modulated Group Relative Policy Optimization (MM-GRPO) (Revised)
PROPOSAL: Modify MM-GRPO to incorporate a novel attention-based mechanism that dynamically weights individual actions within each rollout according to their potential impact on the final outcome. This modification, dubbed "Task-oriented Action Selection" (TAS), will enable the policy to selectively focus on critical steps and discount less relevant ones, thereby providing more informative rewards and facilitating better credit assignment.
CONTROLS: TAS+MM-GRPO with turn-level soft outcome rewards, MM-GRPO with turn-level soft outcome rewards, standard GRPO with outcome-only rewards.
COST: 810 (no change in estimated cost, but increased complexity)
PREDICTION: TAS+MM-GRPO will improve sample efficiency, policy quality, and credit assignment, but may introduce additional computational overhead and require careful tuning of hyperparameters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Intermediate Turn Filtering with Distillation
PROPOSAL: Introduce an intermediate turn filtering mechanism that utilizes a teacher-student distillation framework to identify and suppress unnecessary or suboptimal turns within a rollout. This framework will utilize a pre-trained robust model as a teacher that provides high-confidence preferences over the entire rollout, which will then be used to train a smaller student model to produce a sparse reward signal.
CONTROLS: Student-teacher distillation without filtering (Distilled Rewards), student-teacher distillation with filtering, standard GRPO with outcome-only rewards.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Intermediate Turn Filtering with Distillation will show improved sample efficiency and overall policy performance by eliminating non-informative turns and focusing the policy's attention on the most crucial steps, but may suffer from over-reliance on the teacher model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Reward Redistribution
PROPOSAL: Introduce a hierarchical reward redistribution mechanism that adjusts the rewards received by each turn based on the overall performance of the rollout. This mechanism will utilize a hierarchical framework that allocates more rewards to the earlier turns that are most critical to the final outcome, and less rewards to later turns that are more redundant or unnecessary.
CONTROLS: Standard GRPO with outcome-only rewards, GRPO with hierarchical reward redistribution, GRPO with turn-level soft outcome rewards.
COST: 1080
PREDICTION: Hierarchical Reward Redistribution will demonstrate improved policy quality and credit assignment by providing more nuanced rewards and focusing the policy's attention on the most critical steps, but may introduce additional computational overhead and require careful tuning of hyperparameters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Self-Supervised Sparse Pre-Training for Autonomous Driving
PROPOSAL: Pre-train a 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) model on unlabeled driving data, using the task of monocular depth estimation as a proxy for self-supervision. The 3DGS model projects images onto a 3D volume, and we adjust the rendering depth maps to minimize the error with respect to the ground truth depth maps.
CONTROLS: Compare against a 3DGS model fine-tuned on a supervised depth estimation task.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: I expect this approach to learn useful 3D scene representations, but it may struggle to adapt to new scenes and viewpoints due to the static nature of the pre-training task.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Permutation Equivariant 3D Splatting
PROPOSAL: Design a novel 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) model that is permutation equivariant (PE) with respect to the spatial coordinates of the 3D volume. This is achieved by introducing a permutation invariant network as part of the rendering process. The PE property ensures that the model does not rely on the absolute spatial positions of the projecting images, but rather learns a more general representation that remains invariant under permutations of the images.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the PE property by sampling random permutations of the projecting images and verifying the equivalence of the output representation.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: This design should improve the generalizability of the 3D scene representations, but may require additional computation and may not be applicable to all types of SPMs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer Learning with Task-Adaptive Query Compression
PROPOSAL: Introduce a method to transfer knowledge from a pre-trained model to various query-based SPMs (e.g., sparse 3D object detectors and semantic occupancy predictors) by adapting the query structure to the specific downstream task. The method involves compressing the pre-trained model's queries into a task-adaptive set of queries that better fit the downstream task's requirements, followed by fine-tuning the decoders to optimize the new set of queries.
CONTROLS: Compare against directly fine-tuning the pre-trained model on the downstream task without query adaptation.
COST: 1400
PREDICTION: This approach should improve the performance of the downstream tasks, but the choice of query compression strategy and the optimization of the new set of queries may require significant hyperparameter tuning.

PROPOSAL: Modify the self-supervised pre-training objective to include a loss term that encourages the model to predict the relative pose between consecutive frames. This relative pose information can be used to refine the 3D scene representations and improve the model's robustness to viewpoint changes.
CONTROLS: Compare against the original self-supervised pre-training objective without relative pose prediction.

CONTROLS: Evaluate the quality of the hierarchical representation and its impact on downstream task performance.
COST: 10800
PREDICTION: This hierarchical approach should provide a more comprehensive and robust representation of the scene, but its effectiveness may depend on the design of the hierarchical architecture and the quality of the training data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Online Multitask Learning for SPMs
PROPOSAL: Develop an online multitask learning framework that allows the SPM to learn from multiple related tasks (e.g., object detection, semantic segmentation, and depth estimation) in a sequential and online manner. The framework involves a shared backbone network and task-specific heads, where the backbone network is trained to generalize across tasks and the heads are trained to specialize in specific tasks.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the quality of the learned representations and their transferability across tasks.

PREDICTION: This online multitask learning framework should provide a more comprehensive and adaptive representation of the scene, but its effectiveness may depend on the choice of tasks and the quality of the online training procedure.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Query-Based Sparse Pre-Training with Weak Supervision
PROPOSAL: We propose to leverage weak supervisions (i.e., image-based) derived from self-supervised alignment of neighboring frames in the unlabeled dataset to pre-train a sparse query network. Specifically, we use a combination of optical flow-based alignment and intensity-based consistency checks to estimate the target geometry for masked regions. These estimates are used to regularize the marginal likelihood of the sparse query network, inducing a weak supervisory signal that encourages the model to learn meaningful spatial relationships. We train the network in a geometric augmentation pipeline that perturbs the images with small rotations, translations, and scaling, ensuring robustness to transformations.
CONTROLS: We will pre-train the sparse query network without any task-specific heads or new queries, then evaluate its performance on various downstream SPM tasks such as DETR3D, PETR series, and SparseOcc. We will also analyze the robustness of the generated supervision with respect to the quality of the alignments.
COST: 500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed method will show improved performance on downstream tasks, with a notable boost in geometry-aware capabilities. However, it may fail to learn coherent spatial relationships for scenes with high levels of clutter or occlusion.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Geometry-Aware Query Refining with Scene Flow Guidance
PROPOSAL: To improve the spatial relationships learned by the sparse query network in the first step, we propose to refine its queries using scene flow guidance. We estimate the scene flow (i.e., the motion of objects in the scene) between consecutive frames using optical flow and compute a guidance signal based on this flow. We then add a small query-refining module to the query network that utilizes this guidance signal to adaptively adjust the spatial location of each query. This process is repeated iteratively to refine the query locations, allowing the model to learn more accurate 3D geometric relationships.
CONTROLS: Similar to proposal 1, we will evaluate the model's performance on various downstream SPM tasks. Additionally, we will compare the effectiveness of different scene flow estimation methods (e.g., PWC-Net and RAFT) and guidance signal formulations.
COST: 1200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed query refining module will significantly enhance the spatial coherence of the sparse query network, particularly for scenes with complex motion. However, it may get stuck in local minima due to the iterative refinement process if the initial queries are poorly initialized.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-Modal Consistency for Query-Based Pre-Training
PROPOSAL: To improve the rich spatial-temporal representations learned by the sparse query network, we propose to incorporate cross-modal consistency between the pre-trained query network and a variational autoencoder (VAE) conditioned on the input RGB images. The VAE will predict a probabilistic 3D occupancy map for a given query, and we will add a consistency loss term to ensure that the predicted occupancy maps match the input 2D images through a 2D-3D correlation layer. This encourages the query network to vertex-wise align with the input images, even if the target geometry is 3D.
CONTROLS: The proposed method will be evaluated on various downstream SPM tasks, with a focus on query-based occupancy predictors such as OPUS, SparseOcc, and OSP. We will also compare the effectiveness of different VAE architectures and 2D-3D correlation methods.
COST: 1800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The incorporation of cross-modal consistency will improve the model's 3D representation capabilities, particularly for scenes with significant occlusion or complex geometry. However, it may require a more complex architecture and a much more significant consumption of parameters, which might negatively affect its transferability to other tasks or data sources.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Query-Based Sparse Pre-Training with Adaptive Masking
PROPOSAL: Building upon the first proposal, we modify the sparse query network to use adaptive masking, where the masking strategy (e.g., random or kernel-based) is learned together with the queries. This adaptive masking strategy will allow the network to gather more comprehensive information from the input data by dynamically selecting the most relevant regions. We also incorporate a novel connectionist temporal classification (CTC) based objective that encourages the queries to remain consistent across neighboring frames.
CONTROLS: Similar to the original proposal, we will pre-train the sparse query network without any task-specific heads or new queries, then evaluate its performance on various downstream SPM tasks.
COST: 3000 GPU-hours ( lower estimate, reduced model parameters)
PREDICTION: The adaptive masking strategy will significantly enhance the model's ability to learn meaningful spatial relationships, particularly for complex scenes with diverse textures and structures. However, it may require careful design of the masking strategy and a suitable regularization mechanism to prevent the model from over-compressing the data.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer Learning with Heterogeneous Query-Based Models
PROPOSAL: To address the challenge of transferring knowledge acquired by the sparse query network to heterogeneous query-based downstream models, we propose a domain-based clustering approach to group similar models (based on their query characteristics, decoder architecture, and downstream task) into clusters. We then adapt the query network's knowledge by encouraging the model to focus on the most cluster-relevant queries and adjust the query mapping to align with the downstream model's structure. This adaptation enables the sparse query network to learn a more generalized representation that can be effectively transferred to other downstream models.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate the effectiveness of our approach by comparing the clustering-based and random-index assignments methods on the downstream tasks, using DETR3D and PETR series as examples of heterogeneous downstream models.
COST: 2400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The clustering-based approach will successfully transfer the query network's knowledge to a variety of downstream models, even with different decoder architectures. However, determining the optimal clustering metric and the number of clusters might be challenging, especially for datasets with heterogeneous query characteristics.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Semi-Supervised Query-Based Training with Outlier Detection
PROPOSAL: To address the challenge of acquiring precise ground-truth annotations, especially for real-world driving data, we propose a novel semi-supervised query-based pre-training method that incorporates outlier detection. We utilize a robust 3D reconstruction network to produce potentially incorrect 3D scene reconstructions, which are then classified as inliers or outliers by a separate model. We use the inlier reconstructions as sparse supervisory signals and incorporate outlier detection as a regularization term to avoid fitting noise patterns. This ensures that the sparse query network learns robust 3D scene representations even with imperfect annotations.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate the proposed method on a subset of real-world driving data, labeled with ground-truth and synthetic outliers. We will compare the performance with and without outlier detection, as well as different outlier detection methods.
COST: 3600 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The outlier detection component will significantly enhance the model's robustness to noisy annotations, enabling more effective pre-training with real-world driving data. However, the outlier detection method might not accurately identify real outliers if they have a complex structure or are rare.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Enhanced Cross-Modal Consistency for Query-Based Pre-Training
PROPOSAL: Building upon the third proposal, we refine the cross-modal consistency loss by incorporating a multi-stage attention mechanism to selectively weigh the importance of different 2D-3D correlations. This allows the network to focus more on the most informative regions and reduce the impact of noisy correspondences. Additionally, we introduce a residual connection between the pre-trained query network and a lightweight decoder to facilitate more efficient knowledge transfer and reduce the risk of over-smoothing the query locations.
CONTROLS: Similar to the original proposal, we will evaluate the effectiveness of our enhanced approach on a variety of downstream SPM tasks, such as sparse 3D object detection and semantic occupancy prediction.
COST: 4200 GPU-hours ( higher estimate, increased model complexity)
PREDICTION: The multi-stage attention mechanism and residual connection will significantly enhance the model's ability to learn precise 3D representations and transfer this knowledge effectively. However, the risk of over-smoothing might be higher due to the increased model complexity, requiring careful regularization to avoid detrimental effects on the query locations.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Bootstrap Query Learning for Efficient Knowledge Transfer
PROPOSAL: To improve the efficiency of knowledge transfer from the pre-trained query network to downstream models with different structures, we propose a bootstrap query learning method. We first randomly initialize a subset of queries for the downstream model, then use a gradient-based optimization method to adapt these initial queries to the downstream model's structure. The resulted queries are used to "bootstrap" the pre-trained query network, and a small number of additional queries are added iteratively to update the pre-trained network. This adaptive learning process enables the downstream model to rapidly adapt to the pre-trained query network's knowledge.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate the proposed method on a variety of downstream SPM tasks, comparing its performance with and without the bootstrap query learning process.
COST: 4800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The bootstrap query learning method will significantly speed up the knowledge transfer process, enabling more efficient adaptation of downstream models to the pre-trained query network. However, the choice of initial queries and the number of additional queries added might be crucial for optimal performance and could benefit from careful tuning.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Improved Transfer Learning with Heterogeneous Query-Based Models
PROPOSAL: Building upon the fourth proposal, we refine the domain-based clustering approach by incorporating a degree of hardness metric to assess the similarity between clusters. This metric evaluates the similarity of query features, decoder architectures, and downstream tasks, allowing for more nuanced clustering and enabling the model to better adapt to the most challenging downstream models. Additionally, we introduce a meta-learning component to fine-tune the pre-trained query network for each downstream task, further improving the transferability of knowledge.
CONTROLS: Similar to the original proposal, we will evaluate the effectiveness of our improved approach on a variety of downstream SPM tasks, such as sparse 3D object detection and semantic occupancy prediction.
COST: 6300 GPU-hours ( higher estimate, increased model complexity)
PREDICTION: The degree of hardness metric and meta-learning component will significantly enhance the model's ability to transfer knowledge to a wide range of downstream models, even those with significant differences in query characteristics, decoder architecture, and task requirements. However, the increased model complexity might require careful regularization to avoid over-fitting and detrimental effects on the query locations.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sparse Query Network Generalization through Self-Supervised Domain Adaptation
PROPOSAL: To improve the generalizability of the pre-trained sparse query network across various domains and scenes, we propose a self-supervised domain adaptation approach. We use a series of adversarial training objectives to adapt the pre-trained query network to the target domain's distribution, without using any labeled data from the target domain. We also leverage a novel domain confusion loss to align the feature distributions of the pre-trained query network and the domain-specific query network.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate the proposed method on a variety of downstream tasks, comparing its performance with and without domain adaptation.
COST: 7200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The self-supervised domain adaptation approach will significantly improve the generalizability of the pre-trained sparse query network, enabling it to perform well across various domains and scenes without requiring extensive annotated data. However, the choice of adversarial training objectives and domain confusion loss might be crucial for optimal performance and could benefit from careful tuning.

PROPOSAL: Building upon the fourth proposal, we refine the domain-based clustering approach by incorporating a degree of hardness metric to assess the similarity between clusters. This metric evaluates the similarity of query features, decoder architectures, and downstream tasks, allowing for more nuanced clustering and enabling the model to better adapt to the most challenging downstream models. Additionally, we introduce a meta-learning component to fine-tune the pre-trained query network for each downstream task, further improving the transferability of knowledge.
CONTROLS: Similar to the original proposal, we will evaluate the effectiveness of our improved approach on a variety of downstream SPM tasks, such as sparse 3D object detection and semantic occupancy prediction.

TITLE: Unlabeled Multi-view Driving Dataset via Auto-Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: To exploit unlabeled driving data, we pre-train a lightweight query decoder using auto-contrastive learning on a large-scale unlabeled multi-view driving dataset. Specifically, we add spatial shuffling noise to the input images, and then optimize the query decoder to predict the indices of matching query tokens across different augmented views. This training objective encourages the queries to encode the structural and contextual information from the input views.
CONTROLS: Baseline: no pre-training; Ablation: replacing auto-contrastive learning with DepthFromShading or MaskedAutonencoder projection
COST: 332.5
PREDICTION: The auto-contrastive learning pre-training significantly enhances the spatial coherence of queries; we see improvement in performance on sparse 3D object detection and semantic occupancy prediction when using the pre-trained query decoder versus baseline.

TITLE: QueryDiffusion: Diffusion-based Pre-training for Query-based Sparse Perception Models
PROPOSAL: Inspired by the success of diffusion models in image synthesis, we propose QueryDiffusion, a pre-training method that uses a diffusion process to progressively refine the query tokens in a query-based Sparse Perception Model. QueryDiffusion iteratively applies a learnable diffusion step to the query tokens, refining their representation while maintaining the input's spatial structure.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Cross-Modal Transfer Pre-training for Sparse Perception Models
PROPOSAL: We propose a cross-modal transfer pre-training framework for Sparse Perception Models, wherein we learn a shared representation of scene semantic meaning and spatial layout by leveraging the correlation between RGB images and their corresponding Map Lane Markings (MLMs), obtained from GPS and camera sensors. During pre-training, we project the MLMs onto RGB images to learn a mapping that preserves their layout-related semantics.
CONTROLS: Baseline: no pre-training; Control: comparing our method to FrozenDETR on sparse 3D object detection and semantic occupancy prediction tasks
COST: 834
PREDICTION: The cross-modal transfer pre-training enables sparse perception models to capture rich scene layouts and spatial relationships, ultimately leading to improved performance on tasks such as 3D object detection and semantic segmentation.

This allows the model to encode long-term contextual information, capturing complex spatial structures and contexts.

TITLE: Video-based Pre-training for Sparse Perception Models via Inter-frame Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: We leverage the temporal information from sequential driving footage to pre-train sparse perception models via inter-frame contrastive learning. By maximizing the agreement of query features across adjacent frames while encouraging their disagreement across frames, we allow the model to learn temporally consistent and scene-dependent representations.
CONTROLS: Baseline: no pre-training; Control: comparing inter-frame contrastive learning with auto-contrastive learning and QueryDiffusion on sparse 3D object detection and semantic occupancy prediction tasks
COST: 1400
PREDICTION: The video-based pre-training with inter-frame contrastive learning boosts the model's capacity to capture temporal dynamics and scene structure awareness, leading to improved performance on tasks such as motion prediction and driving scene understanding.

TITLE: Query-Aware 3D Scene Understanding Pre-training
PROPOSAL: Develop a self-supervised pre-training framework for Sparse Perception Models that utilizes a attention-based sparse query alignment module to encourage query-aware representations. Specifically, we introduce a new "Sparse Query Injection" (SQI) loss that rewards the model for correctlyhomeing in on the same sparse query locations when given different views of the same scene. The framework iteratively updates the sparse queries and feature weights to achieve an optimal alignment across multiple views.
CONTROLS: Pre-train and finetune our model on ImageNet-22k, and compare it to a task-agnostic pretrain (TAP) baseline, as well as a frozen pre-trained backbone on ImageNet-22k
COST: 400
PREDICTION: We expect our model to outperform the TAP baseline by 5-7% on a real-world object detection benchmark (e.g. Waymo) and transfer well to downstream tasks such as occupancy prediction, with strong query-awareness and generalization ability. This might fail if the attention mechanism is too simplistic or you over-optimise for query alignment rather than scene understanding.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Attention-Guided Multi-View Feature Fusion
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel feature fusion module (AFM) that uses an attention mechanism to selectively combine multi-view features extracted from different images, promoting adaptive feature resolution and efficient domain adaptation. We propose to use a two-stage attention-based fusion process, where the attention map is first generated based on the semantic similarity between the images, and then the features are fused by element-wise multiplication of the attention map and the feature vectors.
CONTROLS: Evaluate our AFM on the Waymo dataset, comparing it to a naive feature concatenation baseline and a recent multi-view feature fusion method (e.g. Lift-Splat-Shoot).
COST: 600
PREDICTION: We predict that our AFM will improve the detection accuracy of Sparse Perception Models on the Waymo dataset by 3-5%, especially in parts of the images where the semantics of the scenes remain relatively consistent. This might fail if the attention mechanism is too computationally expensive or tends to capture too much irrelevant information.

PROPOSAL: Introduce a new pre-training loss function (STCL) that leverages the temporal structure of driving videos to encourage the Sparse Perception Model to learn robust and generalizable representations. TITLE: Query-Aware 3D Scene Understanding Pre-training
PROPOSAL: Develop a self-supervised pre-training framework for Sparse Perception Models that utilizes a attention-based sparse query alignment module to encourage query-aware representations. Specifically, we introduce a new "Sparse Query Injection" (SQI) loss that rewards the model for correctlyhomeing in on the same sparse query locations when given different views of the same scene. The framework iteratively updates the sparse queries and feature weights to achieve an optimal alignment across multiple views.
CONTROLS: Pre-train and finetune our model on ImageNet-22k, and compare it to a task-agnostic pretrain (TAP) baseline, as well as a frozen pre-trained backbone on ImageNet-22k
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: We expect our model to outperform the TAP baseline by 5-7% on a real-world object detection benchmark (e.g. Waymo) and transfer well to downstream tasks such as occupancy prediction, with strong query-awareness and generalization ability. This might fail if the attention mechanism is too simplistic or you over-optimise for query alignment rather than scene understanding.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Attention-Guided Multi-View Feature Fusion
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel feature fusion module (AFM) that uses an attention mechanism to selectively combine multi-view features extracted from different images, promoting adaptive feature resolution and efficient domain adaptation. We propose to use a two-stage attention-based fusion process, where the attention map is first generated based on the semantic similarity between the images, and then the features are fused by element-wise multiplication of the attention map and the feature vectors.
CONTROLS: Evaluate our AFM on the Waymo dataset, comparing it to a naive feature concatenation baseline and a recent multi-view feature fusion method (e.g. Lift-Splat-Shoot).
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: We predict that our AFM will improve the detection accuracy of Sparse Perception Models on the Waymo dataset by 3-5%, especially in parts of the images where the semantics of the scenes remain relatively consistent. This might fail if the attention mechanism is too computationally expensive or tends to capture too much irrelevant information.

ACTION: ADD 3

PROPOSAL: Design a semi-supervised pre-training framework that leverages scene graph structures to capture spatial-temporal relationships in the scenes, improving Sparse Perception Model's ability to understand complex scene semantics. We will generate scene graphs from unlabeled driving data and use a Graph Contrastive Loss (GCL) to encourage the model to learn consistent scene representations.
CONTROLS: Compare our framework to a supervised pre-training baseline and a state-of-the-art semi-supervised method (e.g. MoCo v3) using a large-scale driving dataset (e.g. nuScenes).
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: We expect our framework to achieve state-of-the-art performance on a sparse 3D object detection benchmark, particularly in scenes with complex object interactions and spatial relationships, and to improve the robustness of the model to open-world variations in the training data. This might fail if the scene graph structures are too noisy or inconsistent, or if the GCL loss is not effective in capturing the complex scene relationships.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learning 3D Geometry from Unlabeled Driving Data Using Context-Aware Sampling
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel pre-training method, SEED (Sparse Entity Embedding Dynamics), which capitalizes on the statistics of unlabeled driving data to learn 3D geometry from multi-view images. Specifically, SEED utilizes a sequence of 3D entity masks, where each entity represents an object or obstacle in the scene, to guide sampling in the 3D space where objects are more densely concentrated. By self-supervised learning, the SEED model aggregates spatial information from sparse entity queries, freeing SPMs from dense BEV computational burdens. In SEED, the sparse queries are learned in an incremental manner, adapting to the context-dependent hierarchical structure of 3D scenes. We will pre-train SEED on the Waymo Open Dataset and evaluate its transfer performance on various SPMs using source code and experiment documentation in Appendices 1 and 2.
CONTROLS: Frozen-DETR pre-trained on ImageNet and DETR3D trained on Waymo with explicit 3D labels.
COST: 16560
PREDICTION: We anticipate large performance gains for 3D object detection tasks across various SPMs, albeit some performance dips for semantic prediction, and expect some difficulty generalizing to extreme weather conditions and low-visibility environments.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Semi-Supervised Pre-Training of SPMs with Few-Label Scenarios
PROPOSAL: We introduce SSLIAM (Semi-Supervised Learning with Implicit Arithmetic Masking), a semi-supervised pre-training approach designed to work with sparse perception models. SSLIAM uses a few labeled images in the pre-training dataset to learn a mask input representation that aligns with the spatial patterns and geometry inherent to the scene, and then drops masking into a view aggregation module (ViAM) that sums the representations of sparse quadruples of images, producing multiple fact-coded views of the scene, freeing models from dense image-volume data loads traditionally plaguing SPM implementations. These representation cycles enable extended inference across the 3D scene without imposing original relational masks on each view. SSLIAM can be adapted for different down-stream applications. 
CONTROLS: SEED, AGASS (original and revised), and Frozen-DETR/DETR3D trained on Waymo with explicit 3D labels.
COST: 27000
PREDICTION: SSLIAM will improve the performance of both 3D object detection and semantic prediction tasks by learning geometry and scene structure under different imaging conditions and expected to outperform AGASS (revised) specifically under scenes involving heavy occlusion.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Probabilistic Hierarchical Knowledge Transfer for Heterogeneous SPMs
PROPOSAL: We propose a probabilistic knowledge transfer framework, PHKT, designed to transfer knowledge acquired from pre-training on unlabeled driving data to various downstream heterogeneous SPMs, such as sparse 3D object detectors and semantic occupancy predictors. PHKT models the uncertainty of the hierarchical scene representations learned from unlabeled data and generates a set of probabilistic hierarchical graphs for each SPM task, adapting to the inference contexts specific to each task.
CONTROLS: SSLIAM, SEED, AGASS (original and revised), and Frozen-DETR/DETR3D trained on Waymo with explicit 3D labels.
COST: 30698
PREDICTION: PHKT will facilitate the transfer of knowledge across different SPM tasks with varying inference contexts, significantly improving task-agnosticness of these heterogeneous models but faces a significant trade-off against increased computational cost that requires definitive causality metrics for real-world deployment.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: 3D Scene Representation via Disentangled Object-Aware Rendering
PROPOSAL: We propose DOR-SPM (Disentangled Object-Aware Rendering for Sparse Perception Models), a novel self-supervised learning framework that uses a 3D disentangled object-aware renderer to learn hierarchical 3D scene representations from multi-view images. DOR-SPM relies on explicit object segmentation and decomposition to selectively render and mask different objects within the scene, effectively learning object-specific features and context-dependent scene structure.
CONTROLS: SSLIAM, SEED, AGASS (original and revised), PHKT, and DETR3D trained on Waymo with explicit 3D labels.
COST: 36000
PREDICTION: DOR-SPM is expected to distinctly improve object recognition and detection across a variety of objects and scenes in the autonomous driving domain without being dull on class-agnostic graph embeddings.

TITLE: Learning 3D Geometry from Unlabeled Driving Data Using Context-Aware Sampling
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel pre-training method, SEED (Sparse Entity Embedding Dynamics), which capitalizes on the statistics of unlabeled driving data to learn 3D geometry from multi-view images. Specifically, SEED utilizes a sequence of 3D entity masks, where each entity represents an object or obstacle in the scene, to guide sampling in the 3D space where objects are more densely concentrated. By self-supervised learning, the SEED model aggregates spatial information from sparse entity queries, freeing SPMs from dense BEV computational burdens. In SEED, the sparse queries are learned in an incremental manner, adapting to the context-dependent hierarchical structure of 3D scenes. We will pre-train SEED on the Waymo Open Dataset and evaluate its transfer performance on various SPMs using source code and experiment documentation in Appendices 1 and 2.
CONTROLS: Frozen-DETR pre-trained on ImageNet and DETR3D trained on Waymo with explicit 3D labels.
COST: 50000
PREDICTION: We anticipate large performance gains for 3D object detection tasks across various SPMs, albeit some performance dips for semantic prediction, and expect some difficulty generalizing to extreme weather conditions and low-visibility environments.

PROPOSAL: We propose AGASS (Annotated Graph Embeddings for Scene Structure), a method to pre-train SPMs on unlabeled driving data by discovering hierarchical scene representations through graph neural network (GNN) node embeddings. AGASS generates graph input representations by projecting SPM queries into onto coarse reconstructions of 3D scene structures and obtaining embedding representations of the node hierarchies using a contrastive representation learning framework. PROPOSAL: We modify AGASS by revising the graph input representation generation step to incorporate explicit contextual information for both scene structure and vehicle interaction. Specifically, our approach uses a graph convolutional network (GCN) to propagate contextual information through node hierarchies, enabling AGASS to model complex vehicle interactions and scene structure changes efficiently. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Semi-Supervised Pre-Training of SPMs with Few-Label Scenarios
PROPOSAL: We introduce SSLIAM (Semi-Supervised Learning with Implicit Arithmetic Masking), a semi-supervised pre-training approach designed to work with sparse perception models. SSLIAM uses a few labeled images in the pre-training dataset to learn a mask input representation that aligns with the spatial patterns and geometry inherent to the scene, and then drops masking into a view aggregation module (ViAM) that sums the representations of sparse quadruples of images, producing multiple fact-coded views of the scene, freeing models from dense image-volume data loads traditionally plaguing SPM implementations. These representation cycles enable extended inference across the 3D scene without imposing original relational masks on each view. SSLIAM can be adapted for different down-stream applications. 
CONTROLS: SEED, AGASS (original and revised), and Frozen-DETR/DETR3D trained on Waymo with explicit 3D labels.
COST: 81000
PREDICTION: SSLIAM will improve the performance of both 3D object detection and semantic prediction tasks by learning geometry and scene structure under different imaging conditions and expected to outperform AGASS (revised) specifically under scenes involving heavy occlusion.

TITLE: Probabilistic Hierarchical Knowledge Transfer for Heterogeneous SPMs
PROPOSAL: We propose a probabilistic knowledge transfer framework, PHKT, designed to transfer knowledge acquired from pre-training on unlabeled driving data to various downstream heterogeneous SPMs, such as sparse 3D object detectors and semantic occupancy predictors. PHKT models the uncertainty of the hierarchical scene representations learned from unlabeled data and generates a set of probabilistic hierarchical graphs for each SPM task, adapting to the inference contexts specific to each task.
CONTROLS: SSLIAM, SEED, AGASS (original and revised), and Frozen-DETR/DETR3D trained on Waymo with explicit 3D labels.
COST: 92000
PREDICTION: PHKT will facilitate the transfer of knowledge across different SPM tasks with varying inference contexts, significantly improving task-agnosticness of these heterogeneous models but faces a significant trade-off against increased computational cost that requires definitive causality metrics for real-world deployment.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Right-Tuning for Source-Free Test-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language Detector
PROPOSAL: We conduct a theoretical analysis of right-tuning, a model-aggregation-based method, for its potential application to source-free test-time adaptation of vision-language detectors. Specifically, we prove that under mild assumptions, right-tuning can be used to obtain an adapted model that minimizes the expected test loss on the target domain. We further demonstrate that this adaptation comes with a computational cost that is linear in the number of samples, making it a promising candidate for real-time adaptation. We experimentally validate our theoretical findings using the standard Faster R-CNN architecture on the COCO validation set.
CONTROLS: We compare our method with state-of-the-art self-training methods, and demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms them on the target domain.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: We expect our method to show improved adaptation performance over self-training methods, especially when the pre-trained detector is sensitive to noise. However, proving the generalization of our approach to more complex architectures is challenging, and adapting right-tuning to more general learning scenarios might be difficult.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: MixMatch-TTA: A MixMatch-Based Test-Time Adaptation Method for Vision-Language Detectors
PROPOSAL: We propose MixMatch-TTA, a test-time adaptation method built upon the MixMatch framework, for adapting vision-language detectors to arbitrary cross-domain and cross-category target data. MixMatch-TTA involves generating pseudo-labels from the target data using a pre-trained detector, and then using these pseudo-labels to mix and match samples from the target and source domains during adaptation. We demonstrate that MixMatch-TTA outperforms state-of-the-art adaptation methods, such as Mini-Titm and TencentTD, on the Visual Genome validation set and the COCO validation set.
CONTROLS: We compare our method with Mini-Titm and TencentTD, and ablate the importance of pseudo-labels, mixing pattern, and online adaptation.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: We expect MixMatch-TTA to achieve state-of-the-art adaptation performance and reduce overfitting by using a combination of pseudo-labels and online adaptation. However, the method may require careful tuning of hyperparameters to achieve good results on challenging datasets.

TITLE: MetaMatch-TTA: A Meta-Learning Based Test-Time Adaptation Method for Vision-Language Detectors
PROPOSAL: We propose MetaMatch-TTA, a meta-learning based test-time adaptation method for adapting vision-language detectors to arbitrary cross-domain and cross-category target data. MetaMatch-TTA learns to adapt the detector's learning rate and regularization schedule to different target domains during meta-training, and then uses these adaptions to fine-tune the detector online during test-time. We demonstrate that MetaMatch-TTA outperforms state-of-the-art adaptation methods on the Visual Genome validation set and the COCO validation set.
CONTROLS: We compare our method with Mini-Titm and TencentTD, and ablate the importance of meta-learning and online adaption.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: We expect MetaMatch-TTA to achieve state-of-the-art adaptation performance and robustness, especially on datasets with significant label noise.

TITLE: Right-Tuning for Source-Free Test-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language Detector
PROPOSAL: We conduct a theoretical analysis of right-tuning, a model-aggregation-based method, for its potential application to source-free test-time adaptation of vision-language detectors. Specifically, we prove that under mild assumptions, right-tuning can be used to obtain an adapted model that minimizes the expected test loss on the target domain. We further demonstrate that this adaptation comes with a computational cost that is linear in the number of samples, making it a promising candidate for real-time adaptation. We experimentally validate our theoretical findings using the standard Faster R-CNN architecture on the COCO validation set.
CONTROLS: We compare our method with state-of-the-art self-training methods, and demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms them on the target domain.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: We expect our method to show improved adaptation performance over self-training methods, especially when the pre-trained detector is sensitive to noise. However, proving the generalization of our approach to more complex architectures is challenging, and adapting right-tuning to more general learning scenarios might be difficult.

TITLE: MixMatch-TTA: A MixMatch-Based Test-Time Adaptation Method for Vision-Language Detectors
PROPOSAL: We propose MixMatch-TTA, a test-time adaptation method built upon the MixMatch framework, for adapting vision-language detectors to arbitrary cross-domain and cross-category target data. MixMatch-TTA involves generating pseudo-labels from the target data using a pre-trained detector, and then using these pseudo-labels to mix and match samples from the target and source domains during adaptation. We demonstrate that MixMatch-TTA outperforms state-of-the-art adaptation methods, such as Mini-Titm and TencentTD, on the Visual Genome validation set and the COCO validation set.

PREDICTION: We expect MixMatch-TTA to achieve state-of-the-art adaptation performance and reduce overfitting by using a combination of pseudo-labels and online adaptation. However, the method may require careful tuning of hyperparameters to achieve good results on challenging datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Test-Time Adaptation for Vision-Language Detectors with Unreliable Pseudo-Labels
PROPOSAL: We propose an online test-time adaptation framework for vision-language detectors, which tackles the challenges of unreliable pseudo-labels and the need for pre-trained knowledge preservation. In each test batch, we select a subset of images with pseudo-labels above a confidence threshold, and apply a partially-connected adaptation mechanism to the pre-trained detector's feature extractor, while freezing its backbone and classification heads. This mechanism allows the detector to adapt to the target domain while preserving its excellent generalization capabilities learned from the source domain.
CONTROLS: We compare our method with a baseline that fine-tunes the entire pre-trained detector on pseudo-labeled target data, and also experiment with different pseudo-label filtering thresholds to understand their impact on adaptation performance.
COST: 8000
PREDICTION: We expect significant improvement compared to the baseline due to effective adaptation of the feature extractor, while preserving pre-trained knowledge. Our method may fail if the pseudo-label filtering threshold is set too high, resulting in reduced adaptation data.

TITLE: Catastrophic Forgetting Mitigation in Test-Time Adaptation for Vision-Language Detectors
PROPOSAL: We investigate the issue of catastrophic forgetting that arises when adapting vision-language detectors to new target domains at test-time. Our approach focuses on minimizing the impact of forgetting while maximizing the adaptation benefit by incorporating a memory-augmented network that stores and retrieves relevant information from a fixed-size memory buffer. This buffer is used to maintain a summary of the previously learned knowledge and reduce the interference between the old and new knowledge.
CONTROLS: We compare our method with the baseline from proposal 1, and also experiment with different memory buffer sizes and retrieval strategies to understand their impact on adaptation performance.
COST: 24000
PREDICTION: We expect improved adaptation performance due to the effective mitigation of catastrophic forgetting, and the ability to maintain a balance between adaptation and preserving pre-trained knowledge. Our method may fail if the memory buffer size is too small, resulting in loss of relevant information.

TITLE: Continual Adaptation with Unsupervised Learning and Label Correction
PROPOSAL: We propose a continual adaptation method that leverages unsupervised learning and label correction to adapt vision-language detectors to new target domains at test-time. In each iteration, our method first uses unsupervised learning to refine the pre-trained detector's feature extractor on the unlabeled target data, and then corrects the pseudo-labels generated by the refined feature extractor to improve the quality of the labels used for adaptation. This process is repeated iteratively, allowing the detector to gradually adapt to the target domain and improve its performance.
CONTROLS: We compare our method with the baseline from proposal 1, and also experiment with different unsupervised learning criteria and label correction strategies to understand their impact on adaptation performance.

PREDICTION: We expect improved adaptation performance due to the effective combination of unsupervised learning and label correction, and the ability to adapt to new target domains iteratively. Our method may fail if the unsupervised learning criterion is too aggressive, resulting in over-adaptation and loss of pre-trained knowledge.

TITLE: Semi-Supervised Test-Time Adaptation using Source-Target Data Pairs
PROPOSAL: We propose a semi-supervised test-time adaptation method that leverages the availability of a few labeled source-domain examples and large amounts of unlabeled target-domain data. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Test-Time Adaptation for Vision-Language Detectors with Unreliable Pseudo-Labels
PROPOSAL: We propose an online test-time adaptation framework for vision-language detectors, which tackles the challenges of unreliable pseudo-labels and the need for pre-trained knowledge preservation. In each test batch, we select a subset of images with pseudo-labels above a confidence threshold, and apply a partially-connected adaptation mechanism to the pre-trained detector's feature extractor, while freezing its backbone and classification heads. This mechanism allows the detector to adapt to the target domain while preserving its excellent generalization capabilities learned from the source domain.
CONTROLS: We compare our method with a baseline that fine-tunes the entire pre-trained detector on pseudo-labeled target data, and also experiment with different pseudo-label filtering thresholds to understand their impact on adaptation performance.
COST: 24000
PREDICTION: We expect significant improvement compared to the baseline due to effective adaptation of the feature extractor, while preserving pre-trained knowledge. Our method may fail if the pseudo-label filtering threshold is set too high, resulting in reduced adaptation data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Batch-wise Self-Training with Sampling and Guided Dent Noise
PROPOSAL: To mitigate the negative effects of unreliable pseudo-labels, we propose modifying the batch-wise self-training process by introducing guided dent noise to the feature extractor's output, whereas dent noise is added to a subset of features only, and their impact on object detection is carefully monitored and controlled. Furthermore, we sample pseudo-labeled images with high-confidence labels to effectively filter out noisy pseudo-labels, and we evaluate the effectiveness of our method in different pseudo-label filtering thresholds and dent noise strengths.
CONTROLS: We compare our method with the baseline from proposal 1, and also experiment with different sampling rates and dent noise schedules to understand their impact on adaptation performance.
COST: 36000
PREDICTION: We expect improved adaptation performance due to the reduction in the impact of noisy pseudo-labels, while preserving the benefits of batch-wise self-training. Our method may fail if the guided dent noise is too aggressive, affecting the detector's overall performance.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Batch-wise Self-Training with Sampling and Guided Dent Noise
PROPOSAL: We refine proposal 2 by incorporating a meta-learning component that learns to adapt to the changing characteristics of the target domain and pseudo-labels at test time. Specifically, we add a meta-learner that takes the pre-trained detector's output and the pseudo-labels as input, and outputs a set of parameters that are used to compute a "quality score" for each pseudo-label. The meta-learner is trained to minimize the distance between the quality score and a label indicating whether the pseudo-label is reliable or not. During test time, the meta-learner is adapted to the current target domain by computing the quality scores for a subset of pseudo-labeled images and using them to filter out noisy pseudo-labels.
CONTROLS: We compare our revised method with the baseline from proposal 1, and also experiment with different meta-learning architectures and optimization schedules to understand their impact on adaptation performance.
COST: 54000
PREDICTION: We expect improved adaptation performance due to the effective filtering of noisy pseudo-labels, and the ability of the meta-learner to adapt to changing target domain characteristics. Our method may fail if the meta-learner is overtrained, resulting in poor generalization to unseen target domains.

TITLE: Self-Learning with Selective-Pseudo Labels for Test-Time Adaptive Object Detection
PROPOSAL: We propose an adaptive object detection framework called SPL-TTAOD (Selective-Pseudo Labels for Test-Time Adaptive Object Detection) that learns from noisy pseudo-labels generated on the fly while selectively utilizing reliable pseudo-labels. SPL-TTAOD employs a novel pseudo-label filtering mechanism using Krull’s conditional similarity and an entropy-based criterion. When reliable pseudo-labels are abundant, our method aggressively updates the model parameters using self-training; otherwise, it resorts to a pre-trained model and adaptively incorporates the，而 (-more info about the update) filtered pseudo-labels. To evaluate the performance of SPL-TTAOD, we will utilize a faster-RCNN-based detector as the backbone network and five standard benchmarks for object detection, including PASCAL VOC 2007, PASCAL VOC 2012, COCO 2014, ImageNet DET 2015, and Aditya sharing benchmarks on e-endxtact: the dex-
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of SPL-TTAOD with the self-learning methods, the pseudo-labeling methods, the previous TTAOD methods, and pre-trained models on the aforementioned datasets. We will also explore the effects of SPL-TTAOD by varying the threshold parameter in the pseudo-label filtering mechanism and perform an ablation study on the components of our method.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: DLM-TTAOD: Domain-Language-Meta Learning for Test-Time Adaptive Object Detection
PROPOSAL: To adapt a vision-language detector to arbitrary cross-domain and cross-category target data, we introduce a Domain-Language-Meta (DLM) learning framework, DLM-TTAOD, for test-time adaptive object detection. DLM-TTAOD consists of three key components: domain confusionlearning, language meta-learning, and adaptive meta-fine-tuning. The domain confusion-learning module alleviates the category space mismatch by learning domain-invariant representations. The language meta-learning module updates the detector's vocabulary by leveraging its language understanding capabilities. The adaptive meta-fine-tuning module efficiently updates the detector's parameters to adapt to the target domain. We will evaluate DLM-TTAOD using a GLIP-based detector, PL-MTL (class imbalance weights), and four real-world benchmarks, including Cityscapes, PASCAL VOC, COCO, and ImageNet DET.
CONTROLS: We will compare DLM-TTAOD with several state-of-the-art TTAOD methods, including SPL-TTAOD (proposed in turn 1) ,pre-trained models, and off-the-shelf object detectors, such as Faster R-CNN and YOLOv3.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: We expect our DLM-TTAOD framework to improve the detection performance under distribution shifts while preserving the detector's pre-trained generalization. Potential failure points may include the high computational costs of the adaptive meta-fine-tuning step and the need for a fine-tuned balance between domain confusion-learning and language meta-learning.

TITLE: VLP-TTAOD: Vision-Language Prompting for Test-Time Adaptive Object Detection
PROPOSAL: Building upon the success of vision-language foundation models, we propose a novel framework, VLP-TTAOD (Vision-Language Prompting for Test-Time Adaptive Object Detection), to adapt a pre-trained vision-language detector to arbitrary cross-domain and cross-category target data. VLP-TTAOD employs a two-stage approach, where we first leverage the pre-trained detector's language understanding capabilities to generate informative visual prompts that highlight discriminative object regions. Then, we adapt the detector using these prompts and the unlabeled target data. To evaluate VLP-TTAOD, we will utilize a Grounding DINO-based detector, a wide range of real-world benchmarks, including COCO, Cityscapes, PASCAL VOC, and ImageNet DET.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of VLP-TTAOD with several state-of-the-art TTAOD methods, including SPL-TTAOD and DLM-TTAOD (proposed in turns 1 and 2, respectively), as well as pre-trained models and off-the-shelf object detectors, such as Faster R-CNN and YOLOv3.
COST: 1400
PREDICTION: We expect our VLP-TTAOD framework to achieve state-of-the-art performance under distribution shifts while preserving the pre-trained generalization of the detector. Potential failure points may include the need for a fine-tuned balance between the generation of informative prompts and the adaptation of the detector.

TITLE: DLM-TTAOD: Domain-Language-Meta Learning for Test-Time Adaptive Object Detection
PROPOSAL: To adapt a vision-language detector to arbitrary cross-domain and cross-category target data, we introduce a Domain-Language-Meta (DLM) learning framework, DLM-TTAOD, for test-time adaptive object detection. DLM-TTAOD consists of three key components: domain confusionlearning, language meta-learning, and adaptive meta-fine-tuning. The domain confusion-learning module alleviates the category space mismatch by learning domain-invariant representations. The language meta-learning module updates the detector's vocabulary by leveraging its language understanding capabilities. The adaptive meta-fine-tuning module efficiently updates the detector's parameters to adapt to the target domain. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Source-Free Adaptation with Sample-Efficient Pseudo-Label Generator
PROPOSAL: We modify a vision-language detector (e.g., GLIP) to leverage a sample-efficient pseudo-label generator (PSEG) at test time. PSEG is developed by combining knowledge distillation and entropy-based pseudo-label screening. The PSEG receives feature embeddings from the GLIP model and outputs pseudo-labels efficiently using a weight- and hyperparameter-reduced external teacher. The GLIP model is fine-tuned on these pseudo-labels but only for a limited number of iterations, preventing overfitting. This adaptive process is repeated during test time to incrementally refine the model's adaptation without relying on source data statistics.
CONTROLS: We will compare to the standard GLIP model and GLIP fine-tuned on synthetic source data for adaptation, while ablating the pseudo-label generator and the fine-tuning procedure to understand their individual contributions.
COST: 1260 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach will show comparable performance to the fully fine-tuned model, but with significantly reduced adaptation time, preserving pre-trained knowledge and staying practical for real-time use.

TITLE: Open-Set Test-Time Adaptation with Adaptive Label Smoothing and Variational Learning
PROPOSAL: To address the challenge of missing pseudo-labels in open-set scenarios, we develop an open-set test-time adaptation framework with adaptive label smoothing and variational learning. A variational approximation of the model's predictive distribution is used to generate a probabilistic pseudo-label, where the label smoothing is adaptively adjusted based on the uncertainty of the model's prediction. We then modify the GLIP model to incorporate a probabilistic feature extraction module that can reason about the uncertainty of its predictions and corrects for overconfidence using the label smoothing technique.
CONTROLS: We compare to the standard GLIP model fine-tuned on synthetic source data, the previous PSEG approach with an additional label smoothing step, and an ablation study on the adaptive label smoothing and variational learning components.
COST: 2165.4 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This framework will achieve better performance in open-set scenarios by effectively handling missing pseudo-labels and reducing overfitting, but may struggle with noisy target data due to the increased uncertainty of the model's predictions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Source-Free Adaptation with Sample-Efficient Pseudo-Label Generator
PROPOSAL: We modify a vision-language detector (e.g., GLIP) to leverage a sample-efficient pseudo-label generator (PSEG) at test time. PSEG is developed by combining knowledge distillation and entropy-based pseudo-label screening. The PSEG receives feature embeddings from the GLIP model and outputs pseudo-labels efficiently using a weight- and hyperparameter-reduced external teacher. The GLIP model is fine-tuned on these pseudo-labels but only for a limited number of iterations, preventing overfitting. This adaptive process is repeated during test time to incrementally refine the model's adaptation without relying on source data statistics.
CONTROLS: We will compare to the standard GLIP model and GLIP fine-tuned on synthetic source data for adaptation, while ablating the pseudo-label generator and the fine-tuning procedure to understand their individual contributions.
COST: 3780 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach will show comparable performance to the fully fine-tuned model, but with significantly reduced adaptation time, preserving pre-trained knowledge and staying practical for real-time use.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Open-Set Test-Time Adaptation with Adaptive Label Smoothing and Variational Learning
PROPOSAL: To address the challenge of missing pseudo-labels in open-set scenarios, we develop an open-set test-time adaptation framework with adaptive label smoothing and variational learning. A variational approximation of the model's predictive distribution is used to generate a probabilistic pseudo-label, where the label smoothing is adaptively adjusted based on the uncertainty of the model's prediction. We then modify the GLIP model to incorporate a probabilistic feature extraction module that can reason about the uncertainty of its predictions and corrects for overconfidence using the label smoothing technique.
CONTROLS: We compare to the standard GLIP model fine-tuned on synthetic source data, the previous PSEG approach with an additional label smoothing step, and an ablation study on the adaptive label smoothing and variational learning components.
COST: 6498 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This framework will achieve better performance in open-set scenarios by effectively handling missing pseudo-labels and reducing overfitting, but may struggle with noisy target data due to the increased uncertainty of the model's predictions.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: (Open-Set Test-Time Adaptation with Adaptive Label Smoothing and Variational Learning)
PROPOSAL: (Revised) To further improve adaptability and generalization, we integrate online domain adaptation techniques into the variational learning framework. A causal effect estimation module is added to the GLIP model to learn the dependency between the source and target domains, allowing for more informed adjustments to the probabilistic pseudo-label generation. The adaptation process is also made more efficient by incorporating momentum-based updating of the feature extraction module.
CONTROLS: The revised framework is compared to the original open-set adaptation approach, the PSEG method, and an ablation study is conducted to investigate the contributions of the causal effect estimation module and momentum-based updating.
COST: 8121 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The revised framework will show improved performance in open-set scenarios and demonstrate better ability to adapt to changing test conditions, but may require additional computational resources due to the increased complexity of the causal effect estimation module.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Composite-Sample-Based Inference
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel sampling technique for test-time adaptation called Efficient Composite-Sample-Based Inference (ECSI). In this approach, we combine the self-training process of pseudo-label generation with a heteroscedastic noise injection technique to obtain robust and high-quality pseudo-labels with efficiently weighted composite samples. The GLIP model is fine-tuned in a manner that leverages these composite samples to adapt to the target domain, leading to improved adaptation performance.
CONTROLS: We compare to the standard GLIP model fine-tuned on synthetic source data and the PSEG method, and evaluate the robustness of ECSI to varying levels of noise in the target domain data.
COST: 9714 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The ECSI approach will show better performance in out-of-distribution scenarios and demonstrate better resistance to noise in the target data, but may require additional computational resources due to the sampling overhead.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: (Open-Set Test-Time Adaptation with Adaptive Label Smoothing and Variational Learning)
PROPOSAL: (Revised) We further investigate the role of self-training and self-supervision in the variational learning framework by integrating a novel self-supervised loss term into the GLIP model. This self-supervised loss helps to reduce the reliance on pseudo-labels and improve generalization to unseen target data. Moreover, a conditional entropy minimization-based pseudo-label shedding strategy is used to handle missing pseudo-labels more effectively, leading to improved robustness and accuracy in open-set adaptation.
CONTROLS: The revised framework is compared to the original open-set adaptation approach, the PSEG method, and an ablation study is conducted to investigate the contributions of the self-supervised loss term and pseudo-label shedding strategy.
COST: 11856 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The revised framework will show better performance in open-set scenarios and demonstrate improved robustness to missing pseudo-labels, but may require careful hyperparameter tuning due to the addition of the self-supervised loss term.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Meta-Learning with Hierarchical Target-Domain Information
PROPOSAL: We propose a meta-learning framework that can adapt to unseen target domains with varying label spaces by learning to reason about hierarchical target-domain information. The framework uses a hierarchical graph-structured neural network to learn a meta-adapter that generalizes to new target domains. The hierarchical graph structure allows the model to capture abstract relationships between target domains and source domain, enabling more effective adaptation in cross-category scenarios.
CONTROLS: We compare to standard meta-learning baselines and also evaluate the performance when the source domain label space is different from the target domain label space.
COST: 14398 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed meta-learning framework will show promising results in adapting to unseen target domains with varying label spaces, but may require significant dataset and computational resources to learn the hierarchical graph structure.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: (Efficient Composite-Sample-Based Inference)
PROPOSAL: (Revised) To enhance the robustness of composite sample-based inference, we integrate a self-supervised contrastive learning module into the GLIP model. This module helps to learn more robust and Wasserstein-debiased composite samples by contrastively enhancing the marginalization of the pseudo-labels generated through composite sampling. We also propose a graph-based clustering approach to automatically select the pseudo-label with the highest credibility for each test image, thus adapting to the varying quality of pseudo-labels.
CONTROLS: The revised framework is compared to the original composite sample-based inference method and an ablation study is conducted to investigate the contributions of the self-supervised contrastive learning module and graph-based clustering approach.
COST: 19176 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The revised framework will show improved robustness and adaptability in handling varying pseudo-label quality and reducing the reliance on any single pseudo-label, but may experience increased computational overhead due to the additional contrastive learning and clustering steps.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Overcoming Adversarial Attacks through Test-Time Adaptation with Isometric Transformation
PROPOSAL: We propose an adaptive approach that resists adversarial attacks through isometric transformation-based test-time adaptation. This approach involves generating robust pseudo-labels that can guide the adaptation of the GLIP model towards more robust and invariant representations. We integrate isometric transformation-based regularization into the self-training process to mitigate the impact of adversarial attacks and improve the overall robustness of the adapted model.
CONTROLS: We evaluate the proposed approach against state-of-the-art robust object detection benchmarks and compare it to other robust adaptation methods.
COST: 21654 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed approach will effectively adapt the model to resist adversarial attacks and improve its robustness, but may experience increased overhead due to the additional regularization step and may not perform as well on non-adversarial tasks due to the modification in the self-training process.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: (Overcoming Adversarial Attacks through Test-Time Adaptation with Isometric Transformation)
PROPOSAL: (Revised) To further improve the robustness of the adapted model, we incorporate a novel self-supervised learning objective that encourages the model to learn disparity-invariant features. This objective involves training the model to predict the disparity between different augmented views of the same image, which promotes the learning of features that are robust to geometric transformations. We also adapt the isometric transformation-based regularization to account for multiple augmentations and evaluate the effectiveness of our approach on more challenging benchmarks with diverse adversarial attacks.

PREDICTION: The revised approach will show improved robustness against diverse adversarial attacks and demonstrate better performance on challenging object detection benchmarks, but may experience increased computational overhead due to the additional self-supervised learning objective and multiple augmentations.
