ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Unified Framework for Multi-Label Image Classification: Combining Adaptation and Transfer Learning
PROPOSAL: We will propose a comprehensive framework for multi-label image classification that leverages the strengths of adaptation and transfer learning. Our framework, called "Multi-Label Adaptation Framework" (MLAF), combines the adaptive component coordination of proposal 1 with the benefits of pre-trained embeddings (proposal 5). We'll also incorporate the class-dependent augmentation strategy from proposal 4 and the efficient inference method from proposal 6. We'll extensively evaluate the performance of MLAF on a diverse set of multi-label image classification datasets.
CONTROLS: We'll compare the results of MLAF to the individual components and combinations (e.g., adaptation only, transfer learning only, adaptation + transfer learning) as well as to the state-of-the-art methods for multi-label image classification.
COST: 33250
PREDICTION: Our framework, MLAF, may establish a new state-of-the-art in multi-label image classification, offering a balanced and adaptable approach that leverages both adaptation and transfer learning. However, we may also find that the complexity of MLAF induces additional challenges, such as an increased risk of overfitting or a higher computational cost for certain datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Online Configuration Tuning for Multi-Label Image Classification
PROPOSAL: We design a reactive approach called NEST (Non-Stationary Environment Solver) that, at each mini-batch iteration, identifies the component in need of tuning (augmentation strategy, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, or loss function) and adaptively adjusts it to improve the model's fitness on the validation set in real-time. NEST's core insight is to invert the loss and augmentation spaces into continuous domains using neural networks, enabling predictive modeling and optimization of the configuration components during training. For example, given an input image and the current augmentation strategy, NEST's predictive model outputs the expected loss under an alternate augmentation scheme. By iteratively sampling from this learned distribution, NEST can explore the augmentation space online, re-weight loss components or modify optimizer parameters dynamically, and re-schedule the learning rate. NEST is an adaptive and reactive strategy that converges within a few thousand iterations and can be combined with existing loss rebalancing or regularization techniques.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: StagyScheduling, Baseline 2: Offline Configuration Search, Baseline 3: Existing Adaptive Techniques (using Learned Augmentation, Adaptive Optimizer, or Cyclical Learning Rate)
COST: 400
PREDICTION: NEST achieves higher validation accuracy and stability on a range of multi-label image classification benchmarks, such as PASCAL-Plus and OpenImages V6, while showing competitive training time and effectively addressing class imbalance and class rarity. Failure may arise from NEST’s sensitivity to hyperparameters such as the dimensionality of the invertible spaces or the strength of exploration.

TITLE: Meta-Model-Based ONLINE Configuration Tuning for Uncertainty Estimation
PROPOSAL: Building upon NEST (proposal 1), we add a meta-model component to effectively estimate the uncertainty associated with the evolving configuration. The meta-model, learned using the validation set in real-time, captures the dependence between the configuration components and their performance. At each mini-batch iteration, this uncertainty proxy guides the online configuration tuning process by Lp-discrepancy criterion from imbalanced to balanced configuration on the uncertain subsets, hence adapting to the evolving multi-label environment, mitigating overconfident estimates, and reaching NGA framework i.e. Novel Geometry Agile. . Moreover, we observe a sudden significant uncertainty rise before the adversary makes discovery. This condition initiates an instant halt of the perturbation of augmentations, resulting in hyper-density leakage within challenging deployment setups tackling end-users' resistance against models’ reliance.

COST: 600
PREDICTION: This extension results in improved validation accuracy, on many heterogeneous imbalance benchmark datasets such as VIMC, ViMM and Corel5k, especially for rare classes. ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Sampling-Based Offline Preprocessing for Enhancing Dataset Representation
PROPOSAL: We introduce a novel offline preprocessing strategy that alters the original dataset representation before inserting it into training pipelines. Instead of optimizing for static configurations directly on unaltered data, we propose a preprocessing step that reduces overfitting, tackles class imbalance and class rarity. Our strategy, dubbed DAR (Data Augmentation Refresher), creates an enriched dataset \(\mathcal{D}'\) by sampling diverse and challenging augmentations, learning varying levels of topical features, and smoothing anomalous cases. This preprocessing enhances the robustness of model fit and test performance, improving convergence speed and adaptability during training. DAR is particularly useful for environments with scarce and noisy class labels or exemplars with disparate relevance to real-world edges.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Techniques that normalize or reweight the training data, such as standardization, whitening, or re-balancing.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: DAR preprocessing offers significant gains in validation accuracy and training speed for multi-label image classification models, especially when faced with rare and imbalanced class labels. However, there's a potential risk of over-augmentation that can lead to overfitting if not carefully controlled.

TITLE: Architecture-Co-Configuration (ACC): Training Multi-Task Models with Dynamic Configuration
PROPOSAL: We introduce Architecture-Co-Configuration (ACC), a novel training strategy that jointly adapts the model's architecture and configuration (data augmentation, optimizer, learning rate schedule, and loss function) to the evolving multi-label classification problem. ACC starts by sampling a subset of relevant model components, and iteratively refines them using a flexible library of architectural patterns and configuration variations. Our method leverages a multi-task learning framework to maintain accurate and efficient configuration, initialization, and adaptation of the adjustable components. By co-adapting the model architecture and configuration, ACC enables learning of more expressive and stable multi-label image classification models, while reducing the need for extensive hyperparameter tuning and expensive re-training.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transparency-Driven Configuration Attainment (TCA): Improving Multi-Label Image Classification via Interpretable Models
PROPOSAL: We propose Transparency-Driven Configuration Attainment (TCA), a framework that integrates model interpretability and configuration adaptation for improved multi-label image classification performance. TCA leverages explainability techniques, such as feature importance scores and model saliency maps, to inform the configuration of the model, including data augmentation, optimization, and loss function. By analyzing the interpretability metrics of the model during training, TCA identifies critical features and regions of the input space that drive errors and adapts the configuration to optimize for these areas. This approach enables the model to develop more accurate and robust representations of the data, reducing overfitting and improving generalization.
CONTROLS: Baselines 1 and 2 from Proposal 3 (Architecture-Co-Configuration), with a control on the interpretability metric used for configuration adaptation (e.g., permutation feature importance vs. SHAP values).
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: TCA improves the model's transparency and accountability, leading to better generalization and a reduced error rate, especially in scenarios where the model is learned from complex, high-dimensional data such as images. However, interpretability metrics may introduce additional computational overhead, and their influence on configuration adaptation requires careful tuning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Auto-Scaling Learning Rate and Data Augmentation for Convergence Acceleration
PROPOSAL: We introduce a novel learning rate and data augmentation scaling strategy that accelerates convergence of multi-label image classification models while maintaining or improving their accuracy. Our Auto-Scaling approach adaptively adjusts the learning rate and data augmentation intensity based on the model's loss function, optimizer, and training dynamics. This is achieved by incorporating a separate neural network, which predicts the optimal scaling factors for the next training iteration, taking into account both the current model's performance and the desired overall convergence speed.
CONTROLS: Baselines 1 and 2 from Proposal 4 (Transparency-Driven Configuration Attainment), with a control on the auto-scaling frequency (e.g., per iteration, every 10 iterations).
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: The proposed Auto-Scaling strategy effectively accelerates convergence without compromising accuracy for multi-label image classification tasks, especially when dealing with large-scale and complex datasets. However, its performance may be sensitive to the initialization of the scaling predictor network, requiring careful hyperparameter tuning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Energy-Based Model Correction for Multi-Label Image Classification
PROPOSAL: We propose an energy-based model correction (EMC) method for multi-label image classification that leverages a separate neural network to produce a correction term for each input sample. The correction term is designed to capture the differences between the model's predictions and the actual labels, allowing for a more accurate and robust classification. During training, the EMC network learns to predict the correction term based on the input image and the model's outputs, and this term is then used to correct the model's predictions. By iteratively refining the energy function, EMC fosters more informed corrections and more reliable classification decisions.
CONTROLS: Baselines 1 and 2 from Proposal 5 (Auto-Scaling), with a control on the EMC network's learning rate and the correction term's weight.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: EMC significantly improves the accuracy and robustness of multi-label image classification models, especially when dealing with rare and noisy labels. However, its performance may be affected by the initialization of the EMC network and the magnitude of the correction term, necessitating careful hyperparameter tuning.

TITLE: Transparency-Driven Configuration Attainment (TCA): Improving Multi-Label Image Classification via Interpretable Models
PROPOSAL: We propose Transparency-Driven Configuration Attainment (TCA), a framework that integrates model interpretability and configuration adaptation for improved multi-label image classification performance. TCA leverages explainability techniques, such as feature importance scores and model saliency maps, to inform the configuration of the model, including data augmentation, optimization, and loss function. By analyzing the interpretability metrics of the model during training, TCA identifies critical features and regions of the input space that drive errors and adapts the configuration to optimize for these areas. This approach enables the model to develop more accurate and robust representations of the data, reducing overfitting and improving generalization.

TITLE: Auto-Scaling Learning Rate and Data Augmentation for Convergence Acceleration
PROPOSAL: We introduce a novel learning rate and data augmentation scaling strategy that accelerates convergence of multi-label image classification models while maintaining or improving their accuracy. Our Auto-Scaling approach adaptively adjusts the learning rate and data augmentation intensity based on the model's loss function, optimizer, and training dynamics. This is achieved by incorporating a separate neural network, which predicts the optimal scaling factors for the next training iteration, taking into account both the current model's performance and the desired overall convergence speed.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Energy-Based Model Correction for Multi-Label Image Classification
PROPOSAL: We propose an energy-based model correction (EMC) method for multi-label image classification that leverages a separate neural network to produce a correction term for each input sample. The correction term is designed to capture the differences between the model's predictions and the actual labels, allowing for a more accurate and robust classification. During training, the EMC network learns to predict the correction term based on the input image and the model's outputs, and this term is then used to correct the model's predictions. By iteratively refining the energy function, EMC fosters more informed corrections and more reliable classification decisions.
CONTROLS: Baselines 1 and 2 from Proposal 5 (Auto-Scaling), with a control on the EMC network's learning rate and the correction term's weight.

However, its performance may be affected by the initialization of the EMC network and the magnitude of the correction term, necessitating careful hyperparameter tuning.

PROPOSAL: We introduce NEST (Non-Stationary Environment Solver), a novel online configuration tuning approach for multi-label image classification that dynamically adjusts the model's configuration to optimize its performance during training. In combination with the previous proposals (Sampling-Based Offline Preprocessing, Architecture-Co-Configuration, Transparency-Driven Configuration Attainment, Auto-Scaling, and Energy-Based Model Correction), NEST forms a comprehensive framework for multi-label image classification that integrates offline and online optimization, interpretable models, and dynamic configuration adaptation.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Adaptive Multi-Label Image Classification via Dynamic Hyperparameter Tuning
PROPOSAL: We propose an algorithm that adaptively adjusts the optimization components (augmentation, optimizer, learning rate, and loss) of a multi-label image classifier at regular intervals during training. These adjustments are based on the current state of the model, including its accuracy and loss on validation data. The algorithm uses a reinforcement learning (RL) agent to learn a policy that trades off exploration and exploitation, balancing the need to avoid overfitting with the need to exploit low-risk configurations.
CONTROLS: We compare our adaptive strategy to a static strategy that uses a fixed set of hyperparameters for the entire training process, as well as an exhaustive search baseline that uses a grid search to find the optimal hyperparameters. We also explore the impact of several key hyperparameters, such as the frequency of adjustments and the capacity of the RL agent.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: Our method should outperform static hyperparameter choices and have a performance profile that adapts more effectively to changing data distributions, but we may encounter challenges in balancing exploration and exploitation, and ensuring that our agent generalizes well to unseen data.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Evaluating the Impact of Inter-Component Interactions on Multi-Label Image Classification
PROPOSAL: To better understand the complex interactions between the different components of a multi-label image classifier, we propose a series of experiments that manipulate and evaluate these interactions. We will create multiple variants of a baseline model, where each variant focuses on a specific combination of augmentation, optimizer, learning rate schedule, and loss function. Our goal is to identify which interactions are critical for optimal performance and determine whether these interactions are consistent across different datasets and models.
CONTROLS: We compare our variants to each other and to a baseline model that uses a standard combination of components, as well as an exhaustive search baseline that finds the optimal combination using grid search. We also analyze the pairwise and higher-order interactions between components to identify potential bottlenecks in the optimization process.
COST: 192
PREDICTION: Our results should provide valuable insights into the complex interactions between the different components of a multi-label image classifier, but the analysis of higher-order interactions may be challenging due to the combinatorial explosion of possible combinations.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Attention-Based Adaptive Loss Functions for Multi-Label Image Classification
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel loss function that adapts to the changing data distribution during training by learning to focus on the most informative labels and samples. Our loss function uses an attention mechanism to assign weights to labels and samples based on their importance, which is learned from the validation data. Our goal is to improve the robustness and efficiency of the training process by focusing on the most relevant parts of the data.
CONTROLS: We compare our adaptive loss function to a set of fixed loss functions, including the standard cross-entropy loss and several state-of-the-art adaptive loss functions. We also explore the impact of different attention mechanisms and label importance metrics on the performance of our loss function.

TITLE: Adaptive Multi-Label Image Classification via Dynamic Hyperparameter Tuning
PROPOSAL: We propose an algorithm that adaptively adjusts the optimization components (augmentation, optimizer, learning rate, and loss) of a multi-label image classifier at regular intervals during training. These adjustments are based on the current state of the model, including its accuracy and loss on validation data. The algorithm uses a reinforcement learning (RL) agent to learn a policy that trades off exploration and exploitation, balancing the need to avoid overfitting with the need to exploit low-risk configurations.
CONTROLS: We compare our adaptive strategy to a static strategy that uses a fixed set of hyperparameters for the entire training process, as well as an exhaustive search baseline that uses a grid search to find the optimal hyperparameters. We also explore the impact of several key hyperparameters, such as the frequency of adjustments and the capacity of the RL agent.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Our method should outperform static hyperparameter choices and have a performance profile that adapts more effectively to changing data distributions, but we may encounter challenges in balancing exploration and exploitation, and ensuring that our agent generalizes well to unseen data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing Effects of Calibration Set Size on PTQ
PROPOSAL: Investigate how varying the size of the calibration set affects the accuracy and variability of PTQ on VGGT for multi-view 3D reconstruction tasks. We will train VGGT on the ScanNet dataset, then perform PTQ using a pre-defined Post Training Quantization algorithm for weights and activations, using different calibration set sizes (e.g. 100, 1k, 10k) sampled from a mixture of scenes with varying types of geometry and lighting. Primary metrics will be mean absolute error in camera pose and 3D point reconstruction accuracy. We will also compare the learned quantization ranges and statistics to assess convergence and variation with calibration set size.
CONTROLS: PTQ using a single fixed calibration set size of 1k, VGGT with full precision
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: As calibration set size increases, PTQ performance will improve, but the marginal gain will diminish. For scenes with larger diversity of geometry and lighting, PTQ performance is more sensitive to the calibration set size. Expect to see larger variance in quantization ranges for smaller calibration sets. The experiments will serve as a starting point for further investigation into more sophisticated calibration strategies and selection methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Robust Calibration Set Selection for PTQ
PROPOSAL: Develop a more robust calibration set selection strategy that can generalize to unseen scenes, particularly for tasks with high semantic complexity like 3D reconstruction. This will be achieved through integration of domain adaptation and entropic regularization. We will employ the recently proposed Meta-Bin framework, which flexibly addresses quantization by balancing the stability of quantization intervals and the accuracy of the model, and fine-tune it using a small meta-learning set composed of diverse scenes. We will then evaluate its performance on PTQ of VGGT on a variety of real-world datasets (e.g. ScanNet, MatterPort3D, 7-Scenes).
CONTROLS: Random selection of calibration sets, Meta-Bin framework without meta-learning for PTQ, full-precision VGGT
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: The new strategy will demonstrate significant improvement in robustness and generalizability over traditional calibration set selection methods. However, high variability in the performance gain across diverse scenes and real-world datasets is expected, highlighting the importance of tailoring the strategy to specific scenes or datasets, as well as pre-training and fine-tuning the framework for domain adaptation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Data-Independent Tokens Handling in PTQ
PROPOSAL: Develop methods to address the unique characteristics of data-independent special tokens (e.g. camera and register tokens) in PTQ of VGGT for multi-view 3D reconstruction tasks. Specifically, we will investigate the use of modified activation clipping and quantization thresholds, constraints on special tokens, and integration of learned scaling factors to normalize token distributions and alleviate heavy tails. We will evaluate these methods using a combination of synthetic and real-world data, focusing on the repartitioning of quantization ranges and the resulting impact on camera pose accuracy and 3D point reconstruction quality.
CONTROLS: Standard PTQ (i.e., using pre-defined quantization ranges and thresholds) without special token handling, standard quantization of VGGT, standard PTQ on 2D vision models without special tokens
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: The proposed methods will demonstrate improved PTQ performance by effectively mitigating the effects of heavy tails in data-independent tokens, with noticeable gains in camera pose accuracy for scenes with challenging settings. However, interpretability concerns and increased computational complexity in some methods are expected, necessitating careful weighting of performance vs speed and overhead.

TITLE: Investigating Data-Independent Tokens Handling in PTQ
PROPOSAL: Instead of modifying activation clipping and quantization thresholds, we will explore an adaptive approach where the learned quantization ranges for data-independent tokens are dynamically scaled based on their statistics. This will be achieved by integrating a learned scaling factor for each special token and its corresponding quantization ranges. We will also investigate prioritizing quantization for the most sensitive special tokens and apply different quantization granularity to reduce information loss while reducing the entropy of token distributions.
CONTROLS: Standard PTQ (i.e., using pre-defined quantization ranges and thresholds) without special token handling, standard quantization of VGGT, standard PTQ on 2D vision models without special tokens

PROPOSAL: Investigate the performance of PTQ with the proposed adaptive handling of data-independent tokens on VGGT for specific challenging scenes and environments, such as those with occlusions, low-light conditions, and dynamic objects. Performance metrics will include both camera pose accuracy and 3D point reconstruction quality, with a focus on evaluating PTQ in different (and potentially more challenging) scenarios.

COST: 46685.4
PREDICTION: Evaluating PTQ on challenging scenes and environments will highlight its sensitivity to complexity and diversity, and provide valuable insights into its limitations and potential for customization based on specific scenes. However, different priorities and trade-offs will be expected for PTQ in various environments, demanding careful tuning of adaptation strategies and prioritization rules.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Knowledge Distillation for PTQ on VGGT
PROPOSAL: Explore the use of knowledge distillation to improve PTQ for VGGT, with the goal of leveraging the fine-grained knowledge of the full-precision model to refine the quantized model's performance. We will use the quantized model as the teacher and fine-tune a smaller, non-quantized student model to mimic the teacher's predictions, then adopt this student model as the PTQ output. By integrating this approach, we aim to reduce the accuracy drop seen after PTQ and adapt it to different scenes and environments.
CONTROLS: Standard PTQ of VGGT, adaptive PTQ with prioritization and dynamic scaling, standard knowledge distillation on 2D vision models
COST: 6600
PREDICTION: Knowledge distillation will provide a sizeable boost in PTQ performance for multi-view 3D reconstruction tasks, demonstrating its potential for recovery of fine-grained details in challenging scenes. However, considerations of computational complexity and overfitting risks will need to be addressed in order for this method to be deployable.

TITLE: Adaptive Bitwidth Policy for PTQ on VGGT
PROPOSAL: Investigate the possibility of adaptively adjusting the bitwidth of different model parameters and quantization ranges during PTQ to better suit the specific characteristics of VGGT and the task at hand. This will involve developing a dynamic bitwidth allocation strategy that balances between representation accuracy, latency, and energy efficiency. We will evaluate the policy on multi-view 3D reconstruction tasks using standard PTQ, adaptive PTQ with dynamic scaling, and knowledge distillation-enhanced PTQ.

COST: 9000
PREDICTION: The adaptive bitwidth policy will be able to dynamically adjust the representation accuracy, latency, and energy efficiency of the PTQ model according to the scene complexity, requiring the model to handle varying inference requirements. While it will introduce additional complexity, dynamic bitwidth control may lead to significant latency improvements in resource-constrained scenarios at the expense of a small sacrifice in model accuracy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Transferability of PTQ Models Across Different 3D Reconstruction Tasks
PROPOSAL: Investigate the transferability of PTQ models trained on one 3D reconstruction task (e.g. camera pose estimation) to another (e.g. point cloud reconstruction or 3D mesh estimation). We will analyze the similarities and differences in the PTQ process across various tasks and investigate whether a single PTQ model can be effectively transferred to different tasks without retraining or fine-tuning. This will help to understand the generalizability and shareability of PTQ models across diverse 3D reconstruction tasks.
CONTROLS: Standard PTQ with task-specific calibration, task-specific PTQ models without model transfer, full-precision VGGT
COST: 10500
PREDICTION: While PTQ model transfer across tasks will likely reveal partial transferability due to the commonalities in point-based representations and shared feature space orthogonality, it will also highlight the task-specific knowledge gaps within PTQ, and specific detailed networks beyond that may involve unique model information in multiple 3D point clouds inference aspects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Promoting Robustness in Multi-View 3D Reconstruction PTQ via Meta-Learning
PROPOSAL: Explore the use of meta-learning for improving PTQ models' robustness in multi-view 3D reconstruction tasks. We will develop a meta-learning framework that adapts to diverse scenes, illumination conditions, and viewpoint changes, and evaluate its performance on PTQ models across various calibrations and model types. This will help to identify the benefits of meta-learning for PTQ robustness and evaluate the transferability of these models to unseen tasks and scenes.
CONTROLS: Standard PTQ models without meta-learning, transfer-learning approaches adapted for PTQ on 2D vision tasks, full-precision VGGT
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: By leveraging meta-learning, PTQ models will demonstrate improved robustness and adaptability across diverse scenes and tasks. However, this will also introduce additional meta-learning overheads, which need to be considered when selecting the optimal meta-trained model for inference. This approach can notably reduce required extensive calibration and hand-tuning on diverse data collections, leaping forward PTQ boosting ability overall on 3D I challenges.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing Effects of Calibration Set Size on PTQ
PROPOSAL: Investigate how varying the size of the calibration set affects the accuracy and variability of PTQ on VGGT for multi-view 3D reconstruction tasks. We will train VGGT on the ScanNet dataset, then perform PTQ using a pre-defined Post Training Quantization algorithm for weights and activations, using different calibration set sizes (e.g. 100, 1k, 10k) sampled from a mixture of scenes with varying types of geometry and lighting. Primary metrics will be mean absolute error in camera pose and 3D point reconstruction accuracy. We will also compare the learned quantization ranges and statistics to assess convergence and variation with calibration set size.
CONTROLS: PTQ using a single fixed calibration set size of 1k, VGGT with full precision
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: As calibration set size increases, PTQ performance will improve, but the marginal gain will diminish. For scenes with larger diversity of geometry and lighting, PTQ performance is more sensitive to the calibration set size. Expect to see larger variance in quantization ranges for smaller calibration sets. The experiments will serve as a starting point for further investigation into more sophisticated calibration strategies and selection methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Robust Calibration Set Selection for PTQ
PROPOSAL: Develop a more robust calibration set selection strategy that can generalize to unseen scenes, particularly for tasks with high semantic complexity like 3D reconstruction. This will be achieved through integration of domain adaptation and entropic regularization. We will employ the recently proposed Meta-Bin framework, which flexibly addresses quantization by balancing the stability of quantization intervals and the accuracy of the model, and fine-tune it using a small meta-learning set composed of diverse scenes. We will then evaluate its performance on PTQ of VGGT on a variety of real-world datasets (e.g. ScanNet, MatterPort3D, 7-Scenes).
CONTROLS: Random selection of calibration sets, Meta-Bin framework without meta-learning for PTQ, full-precision VGGT
COST: 7200
PREDICTION: The new strategy will demonstrate significant improvement in robustness and generalizability over traditional calibration set selection methods. However, high variability in the performance gain across diverse scenes and real-world datasets is expected, highlighting the importance of tailoring the strategy to specific scenes or datasets, as well as pre-training and fine-tuning the framework for domain adaptation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Data-Independent Tokens Handling in PTQ
PROPOSAL: Develop methods to address the unique characteristics of data-independent special tokens (e.g. camera and register tokens) in PTQ of VGGT for multi-view 3D reconstruction tasks. Specifically, we will investigate the use of modified activation clipping and quantization thresholds, constraints on special tokens, and integration of learned scaling factors to normalize token distributions and alleviate heavy tails. We will evaluate these methods using a combination of synthetic and real-world data, focusing on the repartitioning of quantization ranges and the resulting impact on camera pose accuracy and 3D point reconstruction quality.
CONTROLS: Standard PTQ (i.e., using pre-defined quantization ranges and thresholds) without special token handling, standard quantization of VGGT, standard PTQ on 2D vision models without special tokens
COST: 10800
PREDICTION: The proposed methods will demonstrate improved PTQ performance by effectively mitigating the effects of heavy tails in data-independent tokens, with noticeable gains in camera pose accuracy for scenes with challenging settings. However, interpretability concerns and increased computational complexity in some methods are expected, necessitating careful weighting of performance vs speed and overhead.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Investigating Data-Independent Tokens Handling in PTQ
PROPOSAL: Instead of modifying activation clipping and quantization thresholds, we will explore an adaptive approach where the learned quantization ranges for data-independent tokens are dynamically scaled based on their statistics. This will be achieved by integrating a learned scaling factor for each special token and its corresponding quantization ranges. We will also investigate prioritizing quantization for the most sensitive special tokens and apply different quantization granularity to reduce information loss while reducing the entropy of token distributions.
CONTROLS: Standard PTQ (i.e., using pre-defined quantization ranges and thresholds) without special token handling, standard quantization of VGGT, standard PTQ on 2D vision models without special tokens
COST: 10080
PREDICTION: This adaptive scaling and prioritization approach will improve PTQ performance for multi-view 3D reconstruction tasks by accounting for the unique statistics of data-independent tokens and their sensitivity. However, evaluating the potential negative impact of increased model complexity on training and deployment is crucial, and it may be essential to find the right balance between accuracy and efficiency.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Special Token Embeddings on PTQ for VGGT
PROPOSAL: We propose comparing the PTQ performance of VGGT models where the camera and register token embeddings are (1) frozen and (2) fine-tuned on a small auxiliary task that encourages the embeddings to produce a more uniform distribution of values. This will help assess whether tailoring the special token embeddings stimulates better post-training quantization results.
CONTROLS: Full-precision VGGT with fixed and fine-tuned token embeddings as baselines.
COST: 10000
PREDICTION: Fine-tuning the token embeddings may slightly improve PTQ performance, but it will be essential to verify its generalizability across different calibration sets. Conversely, freezing the token embeddings may introduce quantization artifacts if they have non-standard distributions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Calibration Strategy Robustness against Outlier Samples
PROPOSAL: We propose evaluating the robustness of different calibration strategies (e.g., random sampling, class-balanced sampling, uncertainty-based sampling) against samples that are rare outliers in the data distribution. This will involve generating synthetic outlier samples using techniques such as adversarial attacks or rotation augmentation and assessing how well each calibration strategy can detect and mitigate their impact on PTQ performance.
CONTROLS: Calibration strategies without outlier handling as baselines, and a comparative analysis with prior PTQ methods that employed similar calibration strategies in 2D vision tasks.
COST: 13300
PREDICTION: Effective outlier handling could significantly mitigate the degradation of PTQ performance due to rare outliers, and the results will provide insights on adapting existing outlier-handling techniques from 2D vision to multi-view 3D reconstruction tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating PTQ Performance with Different Quantization Schemes and Bit Widths
PROPOSAL: We propose comparing PTQ performance on VGGT across multiple quantization schemes (e.g., uniform, do-re Mi quantization, entropy- based quantization) and bit widths (e.g., 8-bit, 4-bit, 2-bit) to identify the most suitable combination for our specific use case. This will help us to understand the trade-off between quantization accuracy, model size, and computational cost.
CONTROLS: Full-precision VGGT, quantized VGGT using the most common (8-bit uniform) and novel (do-re-mi, entropy-based) quantization schemes, and ablation studies to compare the effect of each scheme on PTQ performance.
COST: 18300
PREDICTION: The chosen quantization scheme and bit width will significantly influence PTQ performance; optimal settings will generally lead to better accuracy, smaller model sizes, and lower computational costs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Special Token Embeddings on PTQ for VGGT
PROPOSAL: We propose comparing the PTQ performance of VGGT models where the camera and register token embeddings are (1) frozen and (2) fine-tuned on a small auxiliary task that encourages the embeddings to produce a more uniform distribution of values. This will help assess whether tailoring the special token embeddings stimulates better post-training quantization results.
CONTROLS: Full-precision VGGT with fixed and fine-tuned token embeddings as baselines.
COST: 30000
PREDICTION: Fine-tuning the token embeddings may slightly improve PTQ performance, but it will be essential to verify its generalizability across different calibration sets. Conversely, freezing the token embeddings may introduce quantization artifacts if they have non-standard distributions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Calibration Strategy Robustness against Outlier Samples
PROPOSAL: We propose evaluating the robustness of different calibration strategies (e.g., random sampling, class-balanced sampling, uncertainty-based sampling) against samples that are rare outliers in the data distribution. This will involve generating synthetic outlier samples using techniques such as adversarial attacks or rotation augmentation and assessing how well each calibration strategy can detect and mitigate their impact on PTQ performance.
CONTROLS: Calibration strategies without outlier handling as baselines, and a comparative analysis with prior PTQ methods that employed similar calibration strategies in 2D vision tasks.
COST: 40000
PREDICTION: Effective outlier handling could significantly mitigate the degradation of PTQ performance due to rare outliers, and the results will provide insights on adapting existing outlier-handling techniques from 2D vision to multi-view 3D reconstruction tasks.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED Exploring Calibration Strategy Robustness against Outlier Samples
PROPOSAL: We propose refining the exploration of calibration strategy robustness by also introducing surrogate tasks that encourage diversity in the sample selection process during calibration. For instance, we can use a multi-objective optimization framework with objectives that balance the desired distribution of calibration samples (e.g., class-balanced) and the diversity of samples (e.g., maximizing the inter-class variance or minimizing the Jensen-Shannon divergence).
CONTROLS: Calibration strategies without surrogate tasks as baselines.
COST: 42000
PREDICTION: By explicitly promoting diversity in the calibration samples, we should be able to improve the robustness of the calibration strategy and reduce the impact of outliers. The specific setup and pre-training data distributions may also reveal whether objectives focused on data variety converge to less optimal calibration sample distributions.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: REVISED Exploring Calibration Strategy Robustness against Outlier Samples
PROPOSAL: We propose refining the exploration of calibration strategy robustness by refining the definition of outliers and considering outliers in different dimensions (e.g., pose, geometry, camera intrinsics) separately. This will help us to evaluate which type of outlier is most challenging for PTQ and which strategy is most robust against that type of outlier.
CONTROLS: Same as before.
COST: 42000
PREDICTION: Focusing on dimension-specific outlier mitigation could facilitate the development of tailored strategies for TPT, as different factors of the data distribution can have inherently different implications for representation and quantization.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating PTQ Performance with Different Quantization Schemes and Bit Widths
PROPOSAL: We propose comparing PTQ performance on VGGT across multiple quantization schemes (e.g., uniform, do-re Mi quantization, entropy- based quantization) and bit widths (e.g., 8-bit, 4-bit, 2-bit) to identify the most suitable combination for our specific use case. This will help us to understand the trade-off between quantization accuracy, model size, and computational cost.
CONTROLS: Full-precision VGGT, quantized VGGT using the most common (8-bit uniform) and novel (do-re-mi, entropy-based) quantization schemes, and ablation studies to compare the effect of each scheme on PTQ performance.
COST: 55000
PREDICTION: The chosen quantization scheme and bit width will significantly influence PTQ performance; optimal settings will generally lead to better accuracy, smaller model sizes, and lower computational costs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Impact of Data-Augmentation on Calibration Set Diversity
PROPOSAL: We propose evaluating the impact of different data augmentation techniques (e.g., random rotation, translation, and flipping, Simulated Multiple Scenarios Using Different camera poses, augmentation of point clouds) on calibration set diversity and PTQ performance. By analyzing the effect of data augmentation on calibration set properties (e.g., class balance, diversity of viewpoint, perspective) and PTQ performance metrics, we can identify optimal data-augmentation strategies for VGGT.
CONTROLS: Baselines without data augmentation, calibration strategies with random sampling and class-balanced sampling.
COST: 58000
PREDICTION: Strategic augmentation of the training set can enhance the diversity of calibration samples and contribute to more accurate and robust PTQ models, as well as episode generalization. Notably testing these hypotheses will require augmenting the POSE datasets popularly used with the small sequence Abdominal+pig et al.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Quantization-aware Pre-calibration of Special Tokens
PROPOSAL: Propose a data preprocessing step to pre-calibrate the special token embeddings, such as the camera token and register tokens, by learning their fine-grained quantization bin boundaries directly from a small validation set. This is done by regressing the bin boundaries using a smaller neural network trained on the validation set, focusing on reducing variability in the distribution of activation statistics from special tokens.
CONTROLS: Compare with standard post-training quantization (PTQ), PTQ with random initialization of special token bins, and PTQ with pre-calibration of image token activations only.
COST: 10000
PREDICTION: Improved robustness and accuracy in camera pose estimation, but potential loss in point cloud reconstruction due to over-tuning of the special token bin boundaries, resulting in reduced generalization across scenes.

PROPOSAL: Propose a novel two-stage, learnable ternary embedding framework for quantizing activations of regular tokens and special tokens, where each embedding is a ternary vector that maps to a binary vector representation using bitwise operations. ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Learnable Cell Map for Bias Compensation in Special Tokens
PROPOSAL: Propose a learnable cell map that allows the model to adaptively compensate for biases in the special token bin boundaries, by learning a compact binary representation of the bin boundaries and using it to correct for biases in the quantization process. This approach enables the model to learn robust and effective bin boundaries that minimize information loss during quantization.
CONTROLS: Compare with PTQ, PTQ with random special token bins, and PTQ with pre-calibration of special tokens, along with a study of learning strategy impact on performance and robustness.
COST: 415000
PREDICTION: Improved robustness and accuracy in camera pose estimation and point cloud reconstruction, but potential overfitting to the learnable cell map and biases in the calibration set, leading to reduced generalization to unseen scenes.

TITLE: Entropy-Based Calibration of Special Token Bin Boundaries
PROPOSAL: Develop an entropy-based calibration approach for special token bin boundaries, which leverages the concept of differential entropy to compute the entropy of each bin and adaptively adjust the bin boundaries to minimize information loss during quantization. This approach aims to improve the model's robustness and generalizability in diverse input scenarios.
CONTROLS: Comparison with existing calibration methods (PTQ, PTQ-R) and ablation studies on different entropy estimation methods and bin boundary adjustments.
COST: 1800000
PREDICTION: Significant improvement in robustness and generalizability of the model, with reduced overfitting to the calibration set and improved accuracy in camera pose estimation and 3D reconstruction tasks, but potential computational cost and scalability issues with large input datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Quantization Ranges for Data-Independent Tokens
PROPOSAL: We will modify the existing VGGT model to include learned quantization ranges for the data-independent special tokens using an additional tiny sub-network, which will adapt to the input data and render the quantization ranges per frame instead of using a common range across all frames. We expect the special tokens to exhibit varying properties across different frames.
CONTROLS: We will compare our approach with the standard PTQ method without learned quantization ranges for the special tokens. We will also include an ablation study where we freeze the learned quantization ranges, i.e., not adapt to the input data, and see the drop in performance due to the limited representativeness of the quantization ranges.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: By adapting the quantization ranges to each frame, we should achieve better preservation of information for the data-independent special tokens, leading to improved accuracy for camera pose estimation and point map reconstruction. The performance might degrade if the learned sub-network fails to generalize across frames or overfits to the calibration data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exponential Quantization for High-Variance Activations
PROPOSAL: Given the vulnerability of uniform and standard quantization methods to extreme activation values exhibited by data-independent special tokens, we will explore the use of exponential quantization, which varies the quantization interval along the log-scale, to reduce information loss. We also consider combining this with a probabilistic masking or winner-takes-all approach to handle extreme outliers while minimizing the loss of representing typical values.
CONTROLS: In addition to comparing with the standard PTQ method, we will also compare with the adaptive quantization range method from proposal 1. We will also experiment with different probability thresholds for probabilistic masking to identify the optimal trade-off between loss reduction and information retention.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: By adapting the quantization scale and employing probabilistic masking or winner-takes-all approaches, we should see a significant reduction in the impact of extreme activation values, and consequently, an increase in the accuracy of 3D reconstruction tasks. However, there is a risk that this method might be overly sensitive to outliers or require proper tuning of its hyperparameters, which could lead to suboptimal performance.

TITLE: Data-Augmentation of Calibration Dataset for 3D Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: To address the concern of biased calibration dataset and rare outliers in the calibration process, we propose to incorporate data augmentation techniques to artificially expand the calibration dataset. This will be done by applying various transformations to the input data, including random translations, rotations, and scaling, to simulate different scenarios and edge cases. We expect this to increase the representativeness and robustness of the calibrated model.
CONTROLS: We will compare our augmented calibration dataset method with the standard validation-only method. We will also examine the impact of different transformation types and intensities on the calibration results.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: By augmenting the calibration dataset, we should see improved robustness and generalizability of the calibrated model across various 3D reconstruction tasks and edge cases. However, there is a risk that overly aggressive data augmentation might lead to overfitting or introduce artifacts in the training data.

TITLE: Uncertainty-Aware Quantization and Calibration
PROPOSAL: To handle the uncertainty inherent in the quantization and calibration process, we propose to incorporate an uncertainty estimation module that computes the confidence in the quantization ranges and calibrated model outputs. This will enable the model to adaptively adjust its quantization ranges and parameter efficiencies based on the confidence levels, potentially leading to improved accuracy and generalizability.
CONTROLS: We will compare our uncertainty-aware method with the standard PTQ and calibration methods. We will also examine the impact of different uncertainty estimation techniques and thresholds on the overall performance.
COST: 1400
PREDICTION: By incorporating uncertainty estimation and adaptive quantization, we should see improved robustness and adaptability of the calibrated model across various 3D reconstruction tasks and edge cases. However, there is a risk that the uncertainty estimation module might introduce overfitting or excessive computational overhead, particularly in low-resource environments.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Knowledge Distillation from VGGT to a Quantized Student Model
PROPOSAL: To transfer the knowledge and capacity of the large-scale VGGT model to a smaller, quantized student model, we propose to use knowledge distillation techniques. The quantized student model will be trained to mimic the output patterns and saliency maps of the VGGT model on a designated set of tasks. We expect this to enable the student model to learn effectively from the VGGT model and adapt to the quantization constraints.
CONTROLS: We will compare our knowledge distillation method with the standard PTQ and calibration methods. We will also examine the impact of different student model sizes and architectures on the overall performance.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: By using knowledge distillation, we should see improved accuracy and generalizability of the quantized student model across various 3D reconstruction tasks, without incurring the computational costs of training a large-scale model like VGGT. However, there is a risk that the knowledge distillation process might lead to information loss or overfitting to the teacher model.

TITLE: Few-Shot In-Context Learning with Self-Supervised Exploration
PROPOSAL: We develop a few-shot in-context learning approach that uses self-supervised exploration to adapt to new environments, leveraging the experience replay buffer as a pool of unlabeled data. This adaptation process is performed solely during inference, without any need for fine-tuning the pretrained model. We will train and evaluate this approach on synthetic data for the experimental domains.
CONTROLS: We compare with a baseline that uses offline fine-tuning and also analyze the efficacy of our approach with and without pretraining on diverse environments.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multistep In-Context Planning for High-Dimensional Action Spaces
PROPOSAL: We propose a multistep in-context planning approach that directly optimizes the sequence of actions within a planning horizon by learning a sequence of probabilistic policies conditioned on the current state and the in-context dataset. This approach is particularly suitable for high-dimensional action spaces, as it can leverage the intermediate steps to refine the action buffer and improve exploration. We will train and evaluate this approach on synthetic data for the experimental domains.
CONTROLS: We compare with the baseline vanilla DreamFusion model and also analyze the tradeoff between planning horizon and exploration-exploitation balance.
COST: 233280
PREDICTION: This proposal should lead to improved exploration and adaptation capabilities in environments with high-dimensional action spaces, but might be computationally expensive due to the sequential optimization process.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Policy Approximation for DPT
PROPOSAL: Reformulate DPT to model the policy as a hierarchical mixture of experts (Mixture of Experts, MoE), where each expert corresponds to a specific MDP structure or task, allowing the model to capture diverse action distributions within a single query.
CONTROLS: Evaluate against vanilla DPT and the previous proposal on a set of tasks from the humanoid control and HVAC control environments in MuJoCo, with a focus on calculating the number of experts required to achieve stable performance and exploring ablations of the hierarchical structure.

PREDICTION: Reduced drift in multi-domain environments, as the model becomes more adept at adapting to task-specific requirements without overwriting general knowledge; potential issue: the equivalence of the hierarchical model to a single MDP structure is unclear, requiring careful care in training and evaluation to avoid overfitting to specific tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Policy Approximation for DPT
PROPOSAL: Reformulate DPT to model the policy as a hierarchical mixture of experts (Mixture of Experts, MoE), where each expert corresponds to a specific MDP structure or task, allowing the model to capture diverse action distributions within a single query.
CONTROLS: Evaluate against vanilla DPT and the previous proposal on a set of tasks from the humanoid control and HVAC control environments in MuJoCo, with a focus on calculating the number of experts required to achieve stable performance and exploring ablations of the hierarchical structure.

PREDICTION: Reduced drift in multi-domain environments, as the model becomes more adept at adapting to task-specific requirements without overwriting general knowledge; potential issue: the equivalence of the hierarchical model to a single MDP structure is unclear, requiring careful care in training and evaluation to avoid overfitting to specific tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scaling DPT to HVAC Control Systems with Multiple Goals
PROPOSAL: We will extend the CNF-based DPT model (proposed in 1) and train it on a collection of synthetic HVAC control tasks mixed from stationary environments. To let the agent learn decision making for multiple goals, we design a new query mechanism and optimization objective in training DPT. This query mechanism will allow for the consideration of competing goals, resulting in a model capable of ranking multiple objectives at inference time.
CONTROLS: Baseline: DPT trained on a single goal for HVAC control.
 Baseline: Reflective random walk policy that blindly chooses the best action in hindsight.
 We'll test and evaluate its performance in real-world simulations for HVAC control systems by considering real-world data input from sensors.
COST: 210
PREDICTION: DPT will learn to generate multiple objective policies that adapt better under various system states and uncertainties in real-world performances which will overcome the baseline that acts naively for single-goal control scenarios.- The discriminative ranking abilities under competing short & long term objective variations need to be thoroughly tested as robustness under task variation.

PROPOSAL: We will adapt the DPT model to use the Conditional Normalizing Flow (CNF) to parametrize and sample from its action distribution. The CNF will allow for a tractable representation of complex, multi-modal action posteriors, enabling actions to be sampled natively at inference time.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scaling DPT to HVAC Control Systems with Multiple Goals
PROPOSAL: We will extend the CNF-based DPT model (proposed in 1) and train it on a collection of synthetic HVAC control tasks mixed from stationary environments. This query mechanism will allow for the consideration of competing goals, resulting in a model capable of ranking multiple objectives at inference time.

TITLE: Intrinsically Disentangled Multi-Task DPT for Generalization
PROPOSAL: Introduce an intrinsically disentangled multi-task objective for the DPT, where each task-specific head is encouraged to learn individual factors that are compositional and robust across tasks. This will help the model capture common latent structures shared across tasks, promoting better generalization and adaptation to novel tasks.
CONTROLS: Original DPT, Multitask-DPT with standard shared weights (ablation)
COST: 750
PREDICTION: This method should improve generalization to unseen tasks and reduce catastrophic forgetting, but may require careful hyperparameter tuning to balance the shared and task-specific components.
